title: Programme History
text: The BSC competition series originated at the University of South Carolina in 1976, under the direction of Dr. John F. Stevens. Since that time, the BAJA Series has grown to become a premier engineering design series for educational Institution teams.

title: BSC Design Series Objective
text:
BSC prepares undergraduate and graduate engineering students in a variety of disciplines for future employment in mobility-related industries by challenging them with a real world, engineering application. Through the Engineering Design Process, experiences may include, but are not limited to:
• Project management, budgeting, communication, and resource management skills
• Team collaboration
• Applying industry Rules and regulations
• Design, build, and test the performance of a real vehicle
• Compete with other students from around the globe
• Develop and prepare technical documentation Students also gain valuable exposure to and engagement with industry professionals to enhance 21st century learning skills, to build their own network, and help prepare them for the workforce after graduation.

title: BSC Objective
text: BSC is an intercollegiate engineering design competition for undergraduate and graduate engineering students. The object of the competition is to simulate real-world engineering design projects and their related challenges. Each team is competing to have its design accepted for manufacture by a fictitious firm. The students must function as a team to design, engineer, build, test, promote and compete with a vehicle within the limits of the Rules. They must also generate financial support for their project and manage their educational priorities. The goal of this programme is to develop well-rounded engineers through hands-on learning.

title: Design Subject
text: Each team's goal is to design and build a single-seat, all-terrain vehicle with maximum speed restricted to 35 km/h, whose driver is contained within the structure of the vehicle. The vehicle is to be a prototype for a reliable, maintainable, ergonomic, and economical production vehicle which serves a recreational user market, sized at approximately 4,000 units per year. The vehicle should aspire to market-leading performance in terms of speed, handling, ride, and ruggedness over rough terrain and off-road conditions. Performance will be measured by success in the static and dynamic events which are described in the BSC Rules and are subject to event-site weather and course conditions.

title: Technical Bulletin
text: A technical bulletin is an informational document released by the BSC on an as-needed basis to communicate problems, issues, or other Rules and safety matters observed during recent competitions.

title: General Notice
text: A general notice is a document released by BSC on an as-needed basis to communicate a clarification or modification of a Rule, process, or safety concern. General notices hold the same validity and weight as the Rule book and are only valid for the competition year in which they are issued.

title: Official Languages
text: The official language of the BSC is English. Document submissions, presentations and discussions in English are acceptable at all competitions in the series.

title: Rules Authority
text: The BSC Rules are the responsibility of the BSC Organising Committee (OC). Official announcements from the BSC Technical Committee (BTC) or the other BSC organisers shall be considered part of and have the same validity as these Rules. Ambiguities or questions concerning the meaning or intent of these Rules will be resolved by the BTC during competition onsite.

title: Rules Variation
text: Rules of BSC are valid for this event.

title: Rules Validity
text: The newest revision of the BSC Rules posted on the website and dated for the calendar year of the competition are the Rules in effect for the competition. Rule sets dated for other years, or older versions of the current year are invalid. For BSC 2027, Rule updates will be provided through WhatsApp.

title: Rules Compliance
text: By entering BSC competition, the team members, Faculty Advisors and other personnel of the entering educational Institution agree to comply with, and be bound by, the Rules and all Rules’ interpretations or procedures issued or announced by BSC. All team members, Faculty Advisors and other educational Institution representatives are required to cooperate with, and follow all instructions from competition organisers, officials and judges. On occasion, BSC representatives encounter designs that comply with the Rules yet have unintended consequences (i.e. hazards, scoring, event efficiency, etc.) that had not been previously considered. BTC shall have the ultimate discretion on what is acceptable at BSC competitions.

title: Rules Comprehension
text: Teams are responsible for reading, understanding and comprehending the Rules in their entirety for the competition in which they are participating. The section and paragraph headings in these Rules are provided to facilitate reading: they do not fully explain all the paragraph contents. Questions regarding the Rules may be submitted by registered users via email to bsc@saeiss.org.

title: Privacy
text: By submitting a Rules inquiry to bsc@saeiss.org, the submitter agrees that both question and the BSC’s answer can be reproduced and distributed by BSC, in edited versions, in any medium or format anywhere in the world. This applies to the written communications made to the BTC. Note: For BSC 2027, all announcements are communicated via email and WhatsApp group created for Participants.

title: Duplication
text: The BTC will answer questions that are not already addressed in the Rules or FAQs or that require new or novel Rule interpretations. For example, if a Rule specifies a minimum dimension for a part, the TCs will not answer questions asking if a smaller dimension can be used.

title: Submission
text: An electronic question submission system has been developed for BSC and available in https://baja.saeiss.org, accessible by logging in through SAEISS Member portal.

title: Documentation
text: Teams submitting questions are required to bring copies of the questions and answers with them to Technical Inspection (TI).

title: Response Time
text: Please allow a minimum of two (2) weeks for a response. The BTC will respond as quickly as possible. However, responses to questions presenting new issues, or of unusual complexity, may take more than two weeks. Note: Please keep in mind that final operating approval of any BSC vehicle can only be given onsite at the competition.

title: Loopholes
text: It is virtually impossible for a set of Rules to be so comprehensive that it covers all possible questions about the vehicle’s design parameters or the conduct of the competition. Please keep in mind that safety remains paramount during BSC, so any perceived loopholes should be resolved in the direction of increased safety of the competition.

title: Participating in the Competition
text: Teams, team members as individuals, Faculty Advisors and other representatives of a registered educational Institution who are present onsite at a competition are “participating in the competition” from the time they arrive at the event site until they depart the site at the conclusion of the competition or earlier by withdrawing. All team members and Faculty Advisors are required to register with their team as part of their Fast Track Roster (Liability Waiver) and obtain a liability wristband at the registration table onsite. The Fast Track Roster can be found on your team profile page at www.sae.org. Your Fast Track Roster must be printed, signed by all team members, and brought to competition after finalised. Please note: All registered team members whether attending onsite or not must be listed.

title: Violations of Intent
text: The violations of the intent of a Rule will be considered a violation of the Rule itself. Questions about the intent or meaning of a Rule may be addressed to BSC staff.

title: Right to Impound
text: BSC organising bodies reserve the right to impound any onsite registered vehicle at any time during a competition for inspection and examination by the organisers, officials and technical inspectors. BSC and the other competition organising bodies reserve the right to impound any safety equipment not meeting the requirements of the Rules. Impounded safety equipment will be held for the duration of the event and will be made available for pickup at the end of the event.

title: General Authority
text: SAEINDIA and the competition organising bodies reserve the right to revise the schedule of any competition and/or interpret or modify the competition Rules at any time and in any manner, that is, in their sole judgment, required for the safe and efficient operation of the event as a whole.

title: Protests and Appeals
text: It is recognized that hundreds of hours of work are put into the design and construction of a vehicle. In the heat of competition, emotions may peak and disputes can arise. The organisers and BTC will make every effort to fully review all questions and resolve problems quickly and efficiently. Note: For BSC 2027, all announcements are communicated via email and WhatsApp group created for participants. The escalation process communicated to the Team leaders and Faculty Advisors are to be followed.

title: Preliminary Review
text: If a team has a question about scoring, judging, policies or any official action it must be brought to the BTC’s attention for an informal preliminary review.

title: Cause
text: A team may protest any Rule interpretation, score or official action (unless specifically excluded from protest) which they feel has caused some actual, non-trivial harm to their team, or has had a substantive effect on their score. Teams may not protest Rule interpretations or actions that have not caused them any substantive damage.

title: Format and Forfeit
text: All protests must be filed in writing and presented to the BTC by the team captain or a designated student team member. In order to have a protest considered, a team must post a twenty-five (25) point protest bond, which will be forfeited if the protest is rejected. Note: BTC, judges or volunteers will not review any video footage as part of the protest.

title: Protest Period
text: Protests concerning any aspect of the competition must be filed within 30 minutes of the end of the event to which the protest relates.

title: Decision
text: The decision regarding any protest is final.

title: Eligibility
text: Eligibility to compete is limited to undergraduate and graduate students to ensure this is an engineering competition rather than a race. Individual members of teams participating in this competition must satisfy the following requirements:

title: Student Status
text: Team members must be enrolled as a degree seeking undergraduate or graduate student in a college or educational Institution. Team members who have graduated during the last seven (7) month period prior to the competition remain eligible to participate.

title: Society Membership
text: Team members must be SAEINDIA members. Proof of membership, such as a membership card, may be required at the event registration and check-in.

title: Age
text: Team members must be at least eighteen (18) years of age at the time of the competition.

title: Driver’s Licence
text: Team members who will drive a competition vehicle at any time during a competition must hold a valid, government issued driver’s licence. All drivers must present their driver’s licence at the time of TI and whenever required by the organisers.

title: Fast Track Liability Waiver
text: All onsite participants and Faculty are required to sign their team’s Fast Track Roster (liability waiver) prior to or upon registering onsite.

title: Insurance
text: Individual medical and accident insurance coverage is required and is the sole responsibility of the participant.

title: Faculty Advisor Status
text: Each team is expected and encouraged to have a Faculty Advisor appointed by the educational Institution. The Faculty advisor is expected to accompany the team to the competition and will be considered by competition officials to be the official Institutional representative.

title: Age
text: Faculty Advisors must be at least twenty-two (22) years of age at the time of the competition.

title: Fast Track Liability Waiver
text: All onsite participants and Faculty are required to sign their team’s Fast Track Roster (liability waiver) prior to or upon registering onsite.

title: Faculty Advisor Responsibilities
text: Faculty Advisors are expected to advise their teams on general engineering and engineering project management theory.

title: Faculty Advisor Limitations
text: Faculty Advisors may not design any part of the vehicle nor directly participate in the development of any documentation or presentation. Faculty Advisors may neither fabricate nor assemble any components nor assist in the preparation, maintenance, testing or operation of the vehicle. Faculty Advisors are not allowed to participate in TI, cost audit or design presentations. The team captain or other designated members of the team must do all the presenting although Faculty Advisors may silently observe. Faculty Advisors may not design, build or repair any part of the vehicle.

title: Student Created
text: The vehicle and associated documentation must be conceived, designed, manufactured, and fabricated by the team members without direct involvement from professional engineers, Faculty, or professionals in the off-road and racing communities.

title: Kit Vehicles Prohibited
text: Vehicles fabricated from a kit or published designs are ineligible to compete. Vehicles which have been professionally fabricated will be disqualified from the competition or receive a penalty.

title: Frame
text: Teams must design, weld, manufacture, and fabricate their frame and all components of the frame. Any professionally fabricated or welded work must be documented on the professional fabrication and manufacturing form, which is part of the Roll Cage Documentation Package.

title: Tubes
text: Any tube(s) that are professionally fabricated must be indicated in the cost report and will be costed at ten (10) times the cost of work completed by the team.

title: Welding
text: Any tubes that are professionally welded must be indicated in the cost report and will be costed at ten (10) times the cost of work completed by the team.

title: Prefabricated Sub-Assemblies
text: These Rules do not exclude the use of prefabricated or modified sub-assemblies made up of commonly available components.

title: Penalties
text: Teams violating any of the Rules in this article will receive a penalty, which depending on the severity of the infraction, could include disqualification from the competition.

text: BSC registration model is “first come, first served” (FCFS) for 2026 edition. The listing of teams is based on the payment date of the first instalment of registration fees.

title: Withdrawals
text: Registered teams will be able to request withdrawal via email to BSC (bsc@saeiss.org). Withdrawals will only be accepted up to four (4) weeks before the event. Registration fees are NOT refundable or transferable.

title: Failure to Meet Deadlines
text:
All teams, both Registered and Waitlisted, for any BSC competition are required to submit all required documents prior to the competition. The required documents provide evidence their vehicle complies with the frame Rules, supports the TI process, and provides material that the Cost and Design event judges need to evaluate the team during the competition. When these documents are not submitted, the judges cannot properly assess the vehicle or the team. Teams that do not submit Cost, Design, Business Presentation, or Technical documents typically do not come to the competition. Teams that do not notify the BSC personnel they are withdrawing from competition create the following problems:
• Teams are still included in the static event schedules and judging time is wasted.
• The unused registration slot cannot be offered to a team on the waitlist. Additionally, failure to submit the required Cost, Design, Business Presentation, and Technical Documents is a clear violation of the Rules. Any blank document submitted to subvert the submission date will be treated as failure to submit. Any document submitted more than five calendar days after the submission deadline shall be classified as “Not Submitted”.

title: General Requirements
text: The vehicle may only use one Rehlko engine of a model specified below for Internal Combustion engine powered BAJA vehicles (ICE BAJA). The vehicle must be capable of carrying one (1) person.

title: Ergonomic Design
text: As a prototype of a commercial product, the design intent must accommodate drivers of all sizes from the 95th percentile male to the 5th percentile female, using the anthropometric references or inspection templates specified by BSC. In addition, the vehicle shall be capable of accommodating a 190 cm, 113 kg occupant as a mandatory design check. All drivers shall meet the roll cage minimum clearances, and fit into a comfortable driving position, while wearing the entire required driver’s equipment. All drivers shall be able to comfortably reach all of the vehicle’s controls. Teams shall be prepared to demonstrate compliance with this requirement in the design event. Teams shall be prepared to demonstrate the compliance to this requirement in the design event.

title: Good Engineering Practices
text: Vehicles entered into BSC competition are expected to be designed and fabricated in accordance with good engineering and construction practices.

title: Terrain Type
text: The vehicle must be capable of safe operation over rough land terrain including obstructions such as rocks, sand, logs, steep inclines up to 45°, mud, and shallow water in any or all combinations and in weather conditions including rain.

title: Clearance and Traction
text: The vehicle must have a minimum static ground clearance of 200 mm and sufficient traction for the terrain type at the competition.

title: Vehicle Configuration
text: BSC vehicle designs shall be unguided ground vehicles (vehicles not requiring fixed guideways) operated by an onboard driver.

title: Wheeled Vehicles
text: Wheeled vehicles with flexible tyres are permitted in BSC. Examples of flexible tyres include pneumatic tyres and flexible “airless” tyres. The vehicle shall have four wheels arranged so that they are not in straight line.

title: Tracked Vehicles
text: Tracked vehicles are not permitted in BSC events.

title: Air Cushion Vehicles
text: Air cushioned vehicles (hovercraft), fan drives (airboats), or other similar designs are explicitly prohibited from competition in BSC events.

title: Drive Type
text: Specialty events such as Suspension, Rock Crawl, or Mud Bog may be designed with specific traction requirements. Teams shall comply with the drivetrain configuration permitted for BSC.

title: Limitations
text: Width: 1626 mm (64 in) at the widest point with the wheels pointing forward at static ride height. Length: Unrestricted. Weight: Unladen Weight to be less than or equal to 250 kg. Note: Teams should keep in mind that BSC courses are designed for vehicles with the maximum dimension of 1626 mm (64 in) width by 2743 mm (108 in) length.

title: Technology Challenge (Innovation)
text: BSC reserves the option to award up to and including 100 bonus points per team who successfully demonstrate specific technologies. If a technology challenge is added, a General Notice will be posted on the https://baja.saeiss.org website prior to the competition registration date of the competition year. There will be no technology demonstrations added after that date for the competition year. The General Notice shall include a description of the technology, guidelines for successful implementation, a timeline for implementation, and a scoring process. The notice will also contain information on any Rules that will be waived or modified for a team that is participating in the technology challenge portion of the competition. The technology challenge will be optional for all teams. BSC will work with sponsors who wish to fund incentives for specific technology challenges. Sponsors shall be required to support the technology demonstration for a minimum of two years. Sponsors shall work with BTC to address any Rules requiring modification to accommodate the technology. Sponsors shall be operationally responsible for the judgement and evaluation of the technology challenge.

title: Required Engine
text: To provide a uniform basis for the performance events, all vehicles shall use the specified engine, modified only as expressly permitted by these Rules and the approved BSC requirements. For BSC, the permitted engine model is Rehlko CH 395-3153.

title: Engine Orders
text: Teams registered for BSC must purchase their discounted engines directly from the identified vendor. The vendor details shall be communicated to teams after the completion of their registration via email. .

title: Additional Engines
text: Teams may purchase additional Rehlko engines directly from the vendor if needed.

title: Hybrid Electric Systems
text: Hybrid-electric drivetrain systems are explicitly prohibited. The use of a starter motor for the purpose of vehicle propulsion is explicitly prohibited.

title: Hydraulic
text: Hydraulic accumulators are the only type of stored energy device that may be incorporated into the vehicle for propulsion purposes. Hydraulic power systems must be properly shielded and documentation of the shielding made available for review. Teams shall provide a hydraulic power specification sheet at the time of TI. The hydraulic power specification sheet is available at https://bajasae.net

title: Kinetic
text: Kinetic energy storage devices, such as flywheels (other than the one inside the engine), are explicitly prohibited.

title: Electric
text: Batteries or other electric energy storage device for vehicle propulsion are explicitly prohibited. Hybrid electric vehicle propulsion systems are explicitly prohibited.

title: Compressed Gas
text: Compressed gas systems for vehicle propulsion are explicitly prohibited.

title: Engine Requirements and Restrictions
text:
The required engine must remain completely stock (except for approved modifications). Approved Modifications

• Charging system installation Note: Blueprinting (reworking an engine to a manufacturer’s exact specifications) is considered to be a modification and is explicitly prohibited. BSC 2027 permits use of OEM supplied fuel tank without any modifications with mentioned Rehlko CH 395-3153.

text: Only Original Equipment Rehlko replacement parts may be used. Consumable parts may be ordered on the Rehlko website: http://www.Rehlkopower.com, procured from a Rehlko dealer.

title: Piston Rings
text: Only standard size, original Rehlko piston rings may be used.

title: Intake Ports
text: No cleaning or removing of aluminium flashing from intake or exhaust ports may be done.

title: Valves
text: Any valve clearance setting between tappet and valve stem may be set. Valves may be lapped to ensure proper sealing. Intake valve seat angle must remain at 45°. Exhaust valve seat angle must remain at 45°.

title: Shafts and Rods
text: The camshaft, crankshaft, connecting rod, and flywheel must not be altered or modified.

title: Spark Plugs
text: The only permitted spark plug is the stock engine sparkplug. No other spark plugs are permitted.

title: Armature
text: Any armature air gap setting is allowed. The armature mounting holes shall not be slotted or elongated to increase or retard ignition timing.

title: Flywheel Rotation
text: The flywheel shall not be rotated to advance or retard timing. The stock Rehlko flywheel key must be used.

title: Engine Governor
text: Each engine is equipped with a speed governor. Each governor shall be set at the competition to 3,750 - 3,800 rpm. Rehlko team shall perform random inspections of the governor on any vehicle, and these may be conducted at any time. Any attempt to defeat the engine governor to increase the engine speed is grounds for immediate disqualification. Caution: Governor setting not to exceed 3,800 rpm.

title: Idle Speed
text: Any idle speed adjustment is allowed, Rehlko recommends 1,800 rpm ± 50 rpm.

title: Air Cleaner
text: The stock air cleaner for a Rehlko 395 - 3153 must be used. Relocation of the air filter is not permitted.

title: High Speed Setting Bracket
text: Changing the high-speed setting bracket is not permitted.

title: Jetting
text: Modifying the Carburettor jet or re-jetting of the Carburettor is prohibited.

title: Float
text: The Carburettor float is not adjustable and may not be modified.

title: Venturi

title: Objective
text: The purpose of the roll cage is to maintain a minimum space surrounding the driver. The cage must be designed and fabricated to prevent any failure of the cage’s integrity during normal operation or during a collision or roll over.

title: Roll Cage Structure
text: The roll cage must be a space frame of tubular steel. The following section outlines the requirements of the physical members and joining methods of the roll cage. Roll cage and Frame Members must be fully welded, and welds must not be ground, sanded or modified so as to prevent inspection. Roll Cage Members and tubes shall not exhibit cutouts, notches, wrinkles, kinks, or any detrimental deformation to the cross-section. Roll cage members and tubes shall be joined by welding the entire circumference and shall not exhibit any injurious defects such as cracking, burn-through, cold lapping, or insufficient penetration. Terminology used in the Rule book relating to the roll cage structure is given below: Frame: The entire tubular structure including required members and non-cantilevered tubes. Roll Cage: Primary and Secondary Members used to protect the driver. Tube: A Primary or Secondary element, which is not required to begin and end at Named Points, except where noted. Member: A Primary or Secondary required element beginning and ending at Named Points. Named Point: The intersection of the centrelines of two or more joining members.

title: Member Requirements
text: Roll cage members shall be made of steel tube and may be straight or bent. Straight members may not extend longer than 1016 mm (40 in) between Named Points. Members exceeding this length shall comply with Rule B.3.2.4 - Additional Support Members. Bent members shall not contain an individual bend greater than 30°. that does not occur at a Named Point; and may not extend longer than 838 mm (33 in) between Named Points or comply with Rule B.3.2.4 - Additional Support Members. Small bend radii (<152 mm or 6 in) that terminate at Named Points are expected, and are not considered to make a member bent, regardless of angle. A bend that terminates at a Named Point implies the point lies at or between the points of tangency of the bend, as shown in Figure B-6. Required dimensions between roll cage members are defined by measurements between member centrelines, except where noted. Junctions of Primary and Secondary members described below must be within 50.8 mm (2 in) of the Named Point, except where noted. Mitred tubing joints of greater than 5° shall be treated as bends. Mitres of less than 5° shall be treated as butt joints and subject to Rule B.3.2.14 - Butt Joints. Required members constructed of multiple members, such as the SIM and LFS, shall be judged as continuous members from Named Point to Named Point, except where noted. Figure B-6: Roll Cage, Bend and Member Termination

title: Primary Members
text:
The required members of the roll cage are illustrated in Figure B-7 and Figure B-8. Members shall always begin and end at Named Points. Tubes, where required, are not required to terminate at Named Points except where noted. Primary members and tubes shall conform to B.3.2.16 - Roll Cage Materials. Primary members are:
• RRH: Rear Roll Hoop Members
• RHO: Roll Hoop Overhead Members
• FBM: Front Bracing Members (Upper, Lower, and Lower when present)
• ALC: Aft Lateral Cross Member
• BLC: Overhead Lateral Cross Member
• CLC: Upper Lateral Cross Member
• DLC: SIM Lateral Cross Member
• ELC: Nose SIM Lateral Cross Member (When Present)
• FLC: Front Lateral Cross Member
• GLC: Nose Front Lateral Cross Member (When Present)
• LFS: Lower Frame Side Members Primary Tubes Are:
• B.3.2.8.1 - Gussets for Lateral Clearance
• B.3.2.12.1 - Gussets for RHO and FBM
• B.3.2.10 - Additional Structure for Driver Toe Protection Figure B-7: Roll Cage, Primary Members (filled in black), Front Braced Frame Figure B-8: Roll Cage, Primary Members (filled in black), Rear Braced Frame

title: Secondary Members and Tubes
text:
Secondary members and tubes shall be of tubular steel, having a minimum wall thickness of 0.89 mm (0.035 in) and a minimum outside diameter of 25.4 mm (1 in) or rectangular steel tubes having a minimum wall thickness of 0.89 mm (0.035 in) and a minimum outside dimension of 25.4 mm (1 in). Secondary members are:
• LDB: Lateral Diagonal Bracing Member(s)
• SIM: Side Impact Members
• FAB: Fore/Aft Bracing Members
• RLC: Rear Lateral Cross Member Secondary tubes are:
• B.3.2.11 - Under Seat Tube (UST)
• B.3.2.4 - Additional Support Tubes
• B.3.2.8.1 - Gussets for Lateral Clearance
• B.4.2 - Any tube used to mount safety belts
• B.6.5.1 - Any tube used to mount the fuel tank
• B.6.5 - Any tube used to protect the fuel system.

title: Additional Support Tubes
text: For bent or straight Primary Roll Cage Members that exceed the maximum allowable length, Additional Support Tubes shall be added. For straight members, a single secondary tube shall connect from the mid-point (+/-127 mm or 5 in) to a Named Point. For bent members, a single secondary tube shall connect from between the tangents of the bend to a Named Point. If Additional Support Tubes are used, the supported Roll Cage Member shall be re-evaluated for length between Named Points and the location of the Additional Support Tube. Primary bent members shall not have a bend greater than 30°. For bent or straight Secondary Roll Cage Members that exceed the maximum allowable length or bend angle, Additional Support Tubes shall be added. For members that exceed only the allowable length OR the allowable bend angle, a single Additional Support Tube is required, with one end connected as described above and the other shall terminate within 2” of a Named Point . For members that exceed both the length AND bend angle limits, two Additional Support Tubes shall connect from between the tangents of the bend to two unique Named Points. Note: As an exception to the definition of Tube in B.3.2.2 – Primary Members and Tubes, Additional Support Tubes shall have one end terminate at a Named Point. Figure B-11: Roll Cage Example, Named Points, Front Bracing

title: LC – Lateral Cross Member
text: Lateral cross members (LC) shall not be less than 203.5 mm (8 in) long. LCs shall not have a bend; however, they may be part of a bent system, provided the minimum length is met between bend tangents. LCs are denoted by the points they connect (e.g. ALC, FLC, etc.). The cross members which connect the left and right points A, B, C, D, F and E/G for ‘Nose’ vehicles (in which case DLC may be omitted) shall be made of primary materials. The LC at Point R for Rear FAB systems may be secondary material and must meet the minimum length described above. Figure B-12: Roll Cage, LC Note: RLC exists only with complete Rear Bracing per B.3.2.13.2

title: RRH – Roll Hoop Members
text:
The RRH is a planar structure behind the driver’s back and defines the boundary between the front- half (fore) and rear-half (aft) of the roll cage. The driver and seat must be entirely forward of this plane. The RRH shall be inclined between 0 and 20° from vertical as viewed from the side of the vehicle. The minimum width of the RRH is 736 mm (29 in), centred on the seat, at a point 686 mm (27 in) seat bottom. The vertical members of the RRH may be straight or bent and are defined as beginning at Point A at the lower end and terminating at Point B at the upper end shown in Figure B- 12. The vertical members shall be continuous from Point A to B (i.e. not multiple segments joined by welding). The vertical members shall be joined by Lateral Crossmembers ALC and BLC at the bottom and top for the RRH. ALC and BLC members must be continuous tubes or adhere to B.3.2.14
- Butt Joints. Points AR/AL, at the lower end of the RRH vertical members, are defined as the intersection with the LFS and ALC. Points BR/BL are defined as the uppermost end of the RRH vertical members. For Roll Cages constructed with bends at the upper end of the vertical members, Point B occurs at the uppermost tangent of the bend. Point B is the intersection of the RRH vertical members with the RHO and BLC. Point B may not reside on the bend or a linear distance from the end of the bend. Note: ALC, BLC, RRH members, LDB and the shoulder belt tube shall all be coplanar. Figure B-13: Roll Cage, RRH

title: LDB – Lateral Diagonal Bracing
text: The RRH must be diagonally braced. The diagonal brace(s) must extend from one RRH vertical member to the other. The top and bottom intersections of the LDB members and the RRH vertical members must be no more than 127 mm (5 in) from points A and B. The angle between the LDB members and the RRH vertical members must be greater than or equal to 20°. Lateral bracing may consist of more than one member. A single straight LDB is exempt from the maximum length in B.3.2.1 - Member Requirements. Figure B-14: Roll Cage, LDB 736.600 mm 68 5. 80 0 m m

title: RHO – Roll Hoop Overhead Members
text: The aft (rearward) ends of the RHO members intersect the RRH within 50.8 mm (2 in) of Points BR and BL (defined by BLC). The forward ends of the RHO members, or the start of the bend between RHO and FBM define points CR and CL (Figure B-12).CLC, BLC and RHO members must all be coplanar. Out-of plane bends at the aft (rearward) ends of the RHO members are not permitted. When a bend is used at Point CR/CL or BR/BL these points are defined at the start of the bend on the top-most plane of the Roll Cage, shown in Figure B-16: Roll Cage, Template Installation. When a bend is used at Point C, CLC must attach at or between the tangents of the bend but shall not be further aft of the start of the bend. The ends of the BLC define the location of points BL and BR. For vehicles constructed with bends at the top of the RRH, point B shall be on the inside end of the bend. Point B may not reside on the bend or a linear distance from the end of the bend. Figure B-15: Roll Cage, RHO Points CR and CL must be between at least 304.8 mm (12 in) forward of a point, in the vehicle’s side view, defined by the intersection of the RHO members and a vertical line rising from the aft end of the seat bottom. This point on the seat is defined by the seat bottom intersection with a 101.6 mm (4 in) radius circle which touches the seat bottom and the seat back. The top edge of the template is exactly horizontal with respect to gravity. Points CR and CL and Points BR and BL must also be no lower than the top edge of the template, 1041.4 mm (41 in) above the seat and shall satisfy the Lateral Space requirements in Rule B.3.3.1 - Lateral Space. Note: The top, longitudinal edge of the template shall be oriented exactly horizontal with respect to gravity. Figure B-16: Roll Cage, Template Installation Figure B-17: Roll Cage Template Drawing

title: Gussets for Lateral Clearance
text: Gussets may be added between the RHO and RRH to satisfy the requirements of Rule B.3.3.1 - Lateral Space. The added tubes shall be of primary material (B.3.2.16 - Roll Cage Materials). Gusset tubes connecting the SIM to RRH or FBM for the purposes of satisfying the requirements of Rule B.3.3.1 - Lateral Space shall be of secondary material (B.3.2.3 - Secondary Members and Tubes. Gussets shall not interfere with the minimum radial clearance required around the fire extinguisher pull knob (B.8.8.5 - Location and Clearance). Tubes governed by this Rule are not subject to bend angle limits in B.3.2.1 - Member Requirements and B.3.2.4 - Additional Support Tubes. Figure B-18: Roll Cage, Gussets

title: LFS – Lower Frame Side Members
text: The Lower Frame Side (LFS) members define the lower right and left edges of the roll cage. These members are joined to the bottom of the RRH at Point A and extend generally forward, to Point F, at least as far forward of every driver’s heel when seated in a normal driving position and actuating the pedals to their full extents. The forward ends of the LFS members are joined by a lateral cross member, FLC (Figure B-11). The intersection of the LFS members and the FLC define the points FR and FL. In ‘Nose’ designs, as shown in Figure B-18, the LFS shall extend forward to Point E, and is joined by lateral cross members FLC and ELC (Figure B-11). Alternative ‘Nose’ designs are feasible wherein Points E and F are co-located, provided adequate foot protection is achieved. Figure B-19: Roll Cage ‘Nose’ Example, LFS

title: SIM – Side Impact Members
text: The two Side Impact Members (SIM) define a horizontal mid-plane within the roll cage. These members are joined to the RRH, defining Point S, and extend forward, to a point at least as far forward of every driver’s toes when seated in a normal driving position. The forward ends of the SIM members shall intersect with the FBM, defining Points DR and DL, this intersection shall be joined by a lateral crossmember, DLC. The SIM members must be between 203 mm (8 in) and 356 mm (14 in) above the inside seat bottom (Figure B-15) at all positions between points S and D. In ‘Nose’ designs, as shown in Figure B-19, the SIM extends forward to Points GR and GL, which shall be joined by a lateral cross member, GLC (Figure B-11). In this case, DLC may be omitted if GLC provides adequate protection for the driver’s toes as noted below. The feet of any driver must be entirely behind the plane defined by points FR/FL and DR/DL. In nose designs the driver’s feet must be entirely behind the plane defined by points GR/GL and ER/EL and below the plane defined by GR/GL and DR/DL. In any design, the structure should provide 25.4 mm (1 in) of clearance between a straight edge applied to any two points on the roll cage and any part of the driver’s foot while actuating all pedals through the full range of motion (See B.7.1.1 - Brake Pedal), If there is insufficient clearance, then an additional structure of secondary material shall be constructed between FBM, SIM and LC members above the driver’s toes when viewed from both the front and side. Figure B-20: Roll Cage ‘Nose’ Example, SIM

title: UST – Under Seat Tubes
text: A secondary tube, or system of secondary tubes, shall pass underneath the seat, positioned in such a way to prevent the driver from passing through the plane of the LFS in the event of seat failure. The UST system shall connect to the LFS members on both sides of the roll cage. The UST may also serve as the mounting location for the seat and/or the anti-submarine belts per B.4.5.3 - Seat Mounting Points and B.4.2.6.3 - Anti Submarine Belt Attachment. Figure B-21: Roll Cage ‘Nose’ Example, UST

title: FBM – Front Bracing Members
text: Front Bracing Members shall join the RHO, SIM and LFS (Figure B-21) at Points C, D and F respectively. The upper Front Bracing Members (FBMUP) shall join Point C on the RHO to Point D on the SIM. It is preferred to notch the SIM around the FBM. The lower Front Bracing Members (FBMLOW) must join point D to point F. The FBMUP and FBMLOW shall each be continuous tubes. The angle between the FBMUP and the vertical must be less than or equal to 45°. If Front FAB, per Rule B.3.2.13.1 - Front Bracing, is used there is no angle requirement between FBM and vertical. Figure B-22: Roll Cage, FBM

title: Gussets for RHO and FBM
text: If the RHO and FBM on one side of the vehicle are not comprised jointly of one tube, bent at point C, then a gusset is required at point C to support the joint between the RHO and the FBM. The total weld length of the gusset must be two times the tubing circumference (of the primary material). Thus, if a tube is used to brace the FBM and RHO, it must be primary material. Plate gussets may be used if the thickness of the material meets or exceeds that of the primary material used. Figure B-23: RHO / FBM Gussets. Figure B-23: RHO / FBM Gussets

title: FAB – Fore - Aft Bracing
text: The RRH shall be restrained from rotation and bending in the side view by a system of triangulated bracing. Triangulation angles (projected to the side view) must be at least 20° between members. Bracing shall either be front bracing or rear bracing (FAB), a better design shall result if both front and rear bracing are incorporated: Rear Bracing - directly restrain both Points B from longitudinal displacement in the event of failure of the joints at Points C; or Front Bracing - restrain both Points C from longitudinal and vertical displacement, thus supporting Points B through the RHO members.

title: Front Bracing
text: Front Bracing systems shall connect the FBMUP to the SIM, on the same sides. The intersection with the FBMUP members shall be within 127 mm (5 in) measured as a straight-line distance from centreline to centreline of Point C. The intersection with the SIM members defines Point P which shall be vertically supported by further members extending from Point P to the LFS members, which defines Point Q. Points P and Q exist only with complete Front Bracing.

title: Rear Bracing
text: Rear Bracing systems shall create a structural triangle, in the side view, on each side of the vehicle. Each triangle shall be aft of the RRH, include the RRH as a vertical element, have one vertex at Point B, and one vertex at either Point S or Point A. The members forming this structural triangle shall be continuous and comply with Rule B.3.2.1. The third vertex is the intersection of these two continuous members and is joined by a Rear Lateral Crossmember (RLC) defining Point R which shall additionally be connected to Point S or A, whichever is not part of the structural triangle. This additional connection, which is required for a complete FAB system, and is not subject to B.3.2.1 - Member Requirements and may be formed using multiple joined members and may encompass a bend of greater than 30°. Attachment of rear FAB system shall be within 50.8 mm (2 in) of Point B, Point S and Point A, on each side of the vehicle. Members connecting to Point A shall attach at an angle of 45° or greater as measured from the ALC. Distances are measured in a straight-line from centreline to centreline of the tube intersections. The aft vertex of each rear bracing triangle defines Point R and shall be joined by a Lateral Crossmember, RLC, per B.3.2.5 - LC – Lateral Cross Member. Figure B-24: Roll Cage, FAB

title: Requirement
text: Many roll cage members are required to be continuous tubes and may not be made of multiple pieces. Roll cage members which are made of multiple tubes, joined by welding in a butt joint, shall be reinforced with an internal sleeve. Tubes which are joined at an angle greater than 5° need not be sleeved; angles of less than 5° shall be considered butt joints.

title: Size
text: Sleeves shall be designed to fit tightly inside the joint being reinforced. External sleeves are not allowed. Sleeves shall extend into each side of the butt joint, a length of at least two times the diameter of the tubes being reinforced and shall be made from steel at least as thick as the tubes being reinforced. Figure B-25: Roll Cage, Butt Joint Sleeve

title: Welding
text: The general arrangement of an acceptable sleeved joint is shown in Figure B-25. A butt weld and four (4) rosette welds are required. Two (2) rosette welds are required on each tube piece. Rosette welds are to be made in holes of a minimum diameter of 15.9 mm (0.625 in). A minimum of 101.6 mm (4 in) of linear weld is required to secure the sleeve inside the joint, including the butt joint and the rosette welds.

title: Welding Process Check
text:
Prior to welding any joint on any of the vehicle’s roll cage elements, each person shall individually complete two welding samples, defined below, using the same primary materials and processes as used in the roll cage element welds. All welding samples shall be submitted at TI. Vehicles for which complete sets of welding samples are not submitted, or for which any of the welding samples are judged inadequate, shall not be allowed to compete in dynamic or endurance events. Welding samples shall be made from the same tube material, diameter, and thickness as the welds made by each person on the primary roll cage elements. For information on best practices for weld samples, see www. bajasae.net/go/downloads. All weld samples shall be indelibly marked, by permanent means such as engraving, etching, or stamping with all the following information:
• School Name or School Initials
• Welder Name or Welder Initials
• Date of construction of weld sample
Sample 1 – Destructive Testing: The sample shall comprise a 90° joint, the leg length of which is unrestricted shall be (Figure B-26) be destructively tested. Passing samples shall exhibit a joint failure in the base material and not in the weld metal. The testing method is free and either tensile or bending failure may be induced; however, the peak stress must be located at the weld. In the case of bending failure, take care that the largest bending moment is located at the weld. Samples shall be tested prior to arrival at competition, and both pieces presented for inspection in the case of complete separation during testing. Figure B-26: Roll Cage, Welding Sample 1
Sample 2 – Destructive Inspection The sample shall comprise of two tubes joined at a 30° angle with a length of at least 149.86 mm (5.9 in) from the centre of the joint (Figure B-27) to the end of each extended leg, and at least 50.8 mm (2 in) on the closed end of the joint. The sample shall be sectioned along the length of tube to reveal adequate and uniform weld penetration (Figure B-27). Samples shall be tested prior to arrival at competition, and both pieces presented for inspection in the case of complete separation during testing. Figure B-27: Roll Cage, Welding Sample 2

title: Roll Cage Materials
text:
The material used for the Primary Roll Cage Members and bracing shall have a specification minimum yield strength of at least 365 MPa and an as-tested carbon content of at least 0.18%. The wall thickness must be at least 1.6 mm (0.062 in) regardless of material or section size. The bending stiffness and bending strength must be calculated about a neutral axis that gives the minimum values.
• Kb minimum: 2620 Nm2
• Sb minimum : 374 Nm Note : Docol R8 tubing is permitted without the required carbon content, provided the aforementioned dimensional requirements or equivalencies are met. This material is not intended to undergo any heat treatment after welding and sizing as this may alter the mechanical properties of the material. Documentation of the materials must include: 1. Invoice(s) of the Primary roll cage materials shall be dated within 5 years of January 1 of the competition year. No exceptions. 2. Material tests or certifications, which specify the carbon content and as-tested yield strength. Manufacturer’s certifications for Primary Material must be dated within 6 years of January 1 of the competition year. No exceptions. 3. For all materials used for Primary material, calculations must be provided proving bending stiffness and bending strength meet or exceed the requirements:
a. Kb minimum: 2620 Nm2
b. Sb minimum: 374 Nm All calculations shall be typed and submitted through the document portal and brought to TI. All calculations shall be in SI units to three significant figures to the nominal tube sizes as specified by the invoice. Bending stiffness, kb, is given by: Where: E - Modulus of elasticity (205 GPa for all steels) I - Second moment of area for the structural cross section Bending strength, Sb, is given by: Where: Sy - Yield strength c - Distance from neutral axis to extreme fibre

title: Roll Cage Specification Sheet
text: Each vehicle must present a completed and signed BSC Roll Cage Specification Sheet at TI. Newly completed copies must be presented for each competition.

title: Lateral Space
text: Minimum space is based on clearances between the driver and a straight edge applied to any two points on the outside edge of the roll cage structure. The driver’s helmet shall have 152.4 mm (6 in) clearance, while the driver’s shoulders, torso, hips, thighs, knees, arms, elbows, and hands shall have 76.2 mm (3 in) clearance. Clearances are relative to any and all drivers selected at TI, seated in a normal driving position, and wearing all required equipment. For any member to contribute to lateral clearance, that member must be listed in B.3.2.2 Primary Members, B.3.2.3 - Secondary Members, or conform to the requirements of B.3.2.8.1 - Gussets for Lateral Clearance or B.3.2.12.1 Gussets for RHO and FBM, otherwise it is assumed to have no contribution (Suspension members, for example, do not contribute to lateral spacing).

title: Vertical Space
text: The driver’s helmet shall have 152.4 mm (6 in) minimum clearance from any two points among those members that make up to top of the roll cage. These members are: the RHO members (exclusive of any covering or padding); the RRH upper, LC; and the LC between points C (left and right). In an elevation (side) view, no part of the driver's body, shoes, and clothing may extend beyond the envelope of the roll cage.

title: Sharp Edges
text: The entire vehicle, including the frame, shall have no exposed sharp edges which might endanger the driver, track workers, or people working around the vehicle while the vehicle is in any attitude (static, dynamic, inverted, etc.).

title: Bolted Roll Cage Joints
text:
Bolted Roll cage joints are acceptable only if the following requirements are met (Figure B-28):
1) Removable members are permitted on non-primary tubes.
2) The tube joint shall be of the design below, constructed to be well-fit and free from injurious defects. Dimensions shown do not include manufacturing tolerances.
3) The only permitted tube sizes for removable members are 25.4 mm (1 in) diameter and 31.75 mm (1.25 in) diameter.
4) The tube joint diameter shall match the diameter of the removable member.
5) The tube joint wall thickness recess shall match the wall thickness of the removable member.
6) Two 6.35 mm (0.25 in) socket head cap screws meeting the requirements of B.12 are required to fasten the tube joint.
7) Nuts used shall meet the requirements of B.12.
8) The tube joint shall be constructed of steel, with a minimum strength requirement matching 1018 steel.
9) Each side of the joint shall have two rosette welds, separated by 180°.
10) Each side of the joint shall be fully welded to the tube of the removable member.
11) Chamfer size C1 shall match the measurement of the wall thickness of the tube.
12) Chamfer size C2 shall nominally be 1.016 mm (0.04 in) Figure B-28: Roll Cage, Required Joint for Removable Members

title: Sleeved Joints
text: Members which need to be drilled through both walls for the purpose of mounting fasteners or routing accessories shall be reinforced with a weld-in sleeve. Sleeves shall be designed to fit tightly on the inside of the hole or joint being reinforced as well as the fastener passing through the sleeve. Sleeves in required members shall be on the tube centreline, have an outer diameter no larger than 0.5 times the member diameter, have a wall thickness greater than or equal to the tube it is welded to and extend beyond the tube on both sides and be fully welded to the tube. An unacceptable joint is denoted by a red “X”. An acceptable joint is denoted by a green “O” in Figure B-28. Figure B-29: Roll Cage, Required sleeve for drilled holes

title: Drilled Holes
text: Single drilled holes in members with a diameter less than or equal to 5 mm (0.197 in) do not require a sleeve.

title: Required Documents
text: Required documents for the Roll Cage Documentation Package include: Roll Cage Specification Sheet & material documentation (invoices, certifications, calculations, etc.) and a single isometric view diagram of the frame highlighting professional fabrication.

title: Document Submission
text:
1) Upload in a Google Drive Folder the Roll Cage Documentation Package
a. Roll Cage Specification Sheet
b. Invoice of roll cage material
c. Material Test of Certification
d. Any Required Calculation per Rule B.3.2.16 - Roll Cage Materials
e. A diagram highlighting any parts of the frame that were outsourced or professionally fabricated
2) Share the link of the files in Google Drive folder during submission for DR 2 via email to bsc@saeiss.org .

title: Process
text: Documents shall be reviewed by the Technical Inspectors on a first come, first serve basis. Typical review period shall be thirty (30) days after the deadline. After review, feedback shall be given to teams. If the submission is rejected by the BSCTI, the team must correct the error noted in the rejection and continue to resubmit the Roll Cage Documentation Package, until they are marked Accepted. It is the responsibility of teams to submit complete documents by the appropriate deadlines. If teams have additional questions, they shall need to use other resources to find the answers or wait until competition.

title: Function
text: The driver restraint system shall function to safely and securely hold the driver within the envelope of the vehicle’s roll cage. The driver restraint system shall also disengage quickly and completely when required to allow the driver a minimum egress time. The driver restraint system consists of a safety harness, arm restraints, and the vehicle’s seat. The driver restraint system shall be fully functional and properly worn whenever the driver is seated in the vehicle.

title: Driver Harness
text: The driver harness shall consist of a 5-point (or more) system comprised of two shoulder belts (left and right), two lap belts (left and right), and one or more anti-submarine belts all joining at a single, central buckle (disconnect point). The anti-submarine belt serves to positively locate the buckle and prevent the driver from riding under the lap belts. Figure B-30: Driver Harness Schematic

title: Certification
text: All driver restraint systems shall meet either SFI Specification 16.5/16.1, or FIA specification 8853/98. The material of shoulder and lap belts shall be of Nylon or Dacron polyester and in new or like-new condition, 76.2 mm (3 in) in width, and free from injurious defects. Anti-submarine belts shall meet the same conditions but have a minimum nominal width of 50.8 mm (2 in). Note: Some 50.8 mm (2 in) anti-submarine belts measure 44.5 mm (1.75 in) actual minimum width and are acceptable for use.

title: Expiration
text: All driver restraints shall have current SFI tags indicating “Valid until:”. Driver restraints may be used provided the valid until date is on or later than the last day of the competition. Figure B-31: Driver Harness, SFI Tag

title: Release Mechanism
text: All belts in the driver harness must join to a single, central, metal-to-metal, lever-type, quick-release buckle. Cam-Lock, and other enclosed buckles susceptible to jamming from small debris (such as sand particles) are explicitly prohibited. The release mechanism (buckle) shall be protected against accidental unfastening from a direct pull, rollover or slide along the side.

title: Shoulder Belts
text: The shoulder harness shall be of the over-the-shoulder type. Only separate shoulder straps are permitted. “Y”-type shoulder straps are explicitly prohibited. Note: Shoulder belt tube shall connect to the RRH vertical members at both ends.

title: Positioning, Vertical
text: The shoulder belt mounting point (A) (see Figure B-30: Driver Harness Schematic) shall be positioned no higher than vertically level with each driver’s shoulders, and no lower than 101.6 mm (4 in) vertically below each driver’s shoulders.

title: Positioning, Lateral
text: The lateral spacing of the shoulder belts shall be between 152.4 mm (6 in) and 228.6 mm (9 in) when measured centre-to-centre. See Figure B-33. Lateral position of the shoulder belts along their mounting tube must be restrained by a structure other than the firewall. Figure B-32: Driver Harness, Shoulder Harness Lateral Position, Overhead view

title: Attachment
text: The shoulder belts shall be looped and secured around a straight, horizontal tube welded within the plane of the RRH. The tube that the shoulder belts are looped around shall meet the requirements of a secondary tube, B.3.2.3 - Secondary Members and Tubes. Provisions for lateral position restraint shall be provided. Firewall material is not acceptable for lateral position restraint. See Figure B-34 for details. Figure B-33: Driver Harness, Shoulder Harness Lateral Restraint Figure B-34: Driver Harness, Diagram of Proper Wrapping of Webbing

title: Redirection
text: The shoulder belts must run directly from their mountings to the driver’s shoulders, without redirection by any part of the vehicle or its equipment, including seats. Webbing shall not be twisted or rotated at any point along the path of the shoulder belt.

title: Adjustment
text: The shoulder belts shall be in proper adjustment for the driver at all times. When the driver harness is worn, each buckle or adjuster in the system shall have excess adjustment capacity to fit all drivers. The minimum length of excess shoulder harness webbing is 101.6 mm (4 in). See Figure B-35.

title: Protection
text: The shoulder belts shall be protected from potential damage from aft of the RRH. The firewall must protect the shoulder belts. The firewall may be pocketed or extended to facilitate this requirement, as long as no open gaps result. Excess shoulder belt webbing shall be neatly contained and kept within the roll envelope of the vehicle.

title: Lap Belts
text: The lap belt halves must run directly from the buckle, over the driver’s hips and to their mounting points without redirection by any part of the vehicle or its equipment (including the seat). The lap belt halves must be mounted to frame tabs using the bracket supplied with the safety harness. Lap belts may not be mounted by wrapping around tubes.

title: Positioning
text: The lap belt (point B to point C) in Figure B-30: Driver Harness Schematic shall be positioned such that it passes over the driver’s pelvic area below the Anterior Superior Iliac Spines (the hip bones). The lap belt shall not be worn over the driver’s intestines or abdomen. In a side view, the lap belt must be at a minor angle (angle “L” or angle BCD) of between 45° and 80° to the horizontal. This requirement means that the centreline of the lap belt at the seat bottom shall be approximately 76.2 mm (3 in) forward of the bottom of the seat back. Figure B-35: Driver Harness, Lap Belt Angle

title: Attachment
text: The lap belts shall be securely attached to the vehicle frame with threaded fasteners and metal tabs meeting the requirements of B.12.2 - Required Attachment Tabs. Tabs shall be attached to primary or secondary tubes in the plane of the LFS or RRH. Webbing shall be routed through buckles per Figure B-35. The frame lap belt tabs shall be installed such that the lap belt tabs pivot freely and are not loaded in bending. Lap belts wrapped around tubes or secured with eye-bolts and/or eye-bolt hardware are explicitly prohibited. Lap belts shall be fastened to the vehicle frame with bolts no less than 11.113 mm (7/16 in) in diameter. Figure B-36: Driver Harness, Lap Belt Tab Orientation

title: Redirection
text: The lap belts shall be routed directly from the mounting points over the driver’s hips and to the release mechanism (buckle) without redirection by any part of the vehicle or its equipment (including the seat). Webbing shall not be twisted or rotated at any point along the path of the lap belt.

title: Adjustment
text: The lap belts shall be in proper adjustment for the driver at all times. When the driver harness is worn, each buckle or adjuster in the system shall have excess adjustment capacity. The minimum length of excess lap belt webbing is 101.6 mm (4 in). See Figure B-35.

title: Protection
text: The lap belts shall be protected from potential damage by the vehicle’s body panels. Excess lap belt webbing shall be neatly contained and kept within the roll envelope of the vehicle.

title: Number of Points
text: The anti-submarine belt (Line BD in Figure B-30: Driver Harness Schematic) shall be at least a single-point mount (a 5-point driver harness configuration). Driver harnesses of the 6-point and 7- point types are permitted. A 6-point system utilises two anti-submarine belt mounting points. A 7-point system utilises three anti-submarine belt mounting points.

title: Positioning
text: Anti-submarine belts shall be mounted to the vehicle frame at a point aft of the chest line as denoted by a positive angle “S” in Figure B-30: Driver Harness Schematic. The anti-submarine belt mounting point shall be forward of the lap belt mounting points. The chest line passes through point B and is parallel to the driver’s sternum. The anti-submarine belt angle (angle S) is suggested to be 20°. The anti-submarine belt shall be mounted either to a frame tab or wrapped around a frame member meeting at least secondary member requirement. 6-point and 7-point harnesses shall be installed as per the manufacturer’s instructions. Teams shall be prepared to provide documentation of mounting instructions to Technical Inspectors at the time of TI.

title: Attachment
text:
The anti-submarine belts shall be securely attached to the vehicle frame by one of the following methods:
a. Metal tabs joined by a threaded fastener.
b. Webbing wrapped around a frame member
c. Webbing wrapped around a bolt secured by metal tabs in double shear. Anti-submarine belts secured with eye-bolts are explicitly prohibited. Webbing shall be wrapped per Figure B-35: Driver Harness, Diagram of Proper Wrapping of Webbing. Any threaded fastener in the driver restraint system shall meet the requirements of Part B : Article 12
- Fasteners. Anti-submarine belts, if bolted, shall be fastened to the vehicle frame with bolts no less than 11.11 mm (7/16 in) in diameter. The frame tabs which accept the metal anti-submarine belt tabs or bolt in method “a” or “c” shall meet the following requirements of B.12.2 - Required Attachment Tabs. If the anti-submarine belt is wrapped around a frame member (method “b”) or a bolt (method “c”), the following requirements shall be met:
a. The anti-submarine belt mounting tube shall have features designed to limit total lateral movement to 25.4 mm (1 in) or less.
b. The anti-submarine belt webbing shall be protected from sharp edges such as bolt threads, tab edges, and
c. The anti-submarine belt mounting tube or tube holding tabs shall meet the frame requirements of a secondary member. The mounting tube may be constructed of a single tube with bends or may be constructed with no more than three tubes and two mitered joints (excluding connections to the LFS). The anti-submarine belt mounting tube shall join both of the vehicle’s LFS members and be oriented parallel to the LC’s. The mounting tube may not be cantilevered off of another tube creating an undue bending moment.

title: Redirection
text: Redirection of the anti-submarine belt by a rigid frame, seat member, or seat edge is allowed. Redirected belt webbing must not contain a bend of more than 30° (Figure B-39). The redirecting member or edge must be designed to prevent chafing or abrasion of the belt webbing. Webbing shall not be twisted at any point along the path of the anti-submarine belt. Point of Figure B-37: Driver Harness, Anti-Submarine Belt Redirection

title: Adjustment
text: The anti-submarine belts shall be in proper adjustment for the driver at all times. When the driver harness is worn, each buckle or adjuster in the system shall have excess adjustment capacity.

title: Protection
text: All anti-submarine belts shall be protected by the vehicle skid plate. Excess anti-submarine belt webbing shall be neatly contained and kept within the roll envelope of the vehicle.

title: Arm Restraints
text: All drivers are required to wear SFI 3.3 arm restraints to keep the driver’s arms within the roll cage in the event of a rollover.

title: Condition
text: The restraints must be in overall good condition and show no signs of wear, no cuts, fretting, chafing or wear. The restraints must bear the appropriate labels. Point of Release Attachment Point of Redirection Frame Attachment Angle <=30 ° Figure B-38: Driver Harness, Arm Restraints

title: Expiration
text: Arm restraint expiration dates are not required.

title: Positioning
text: The arm restraints must be worn by the driver on the forearm just below the elbow. The driver must be able to reach the cockpit kill switch and release the harness buckle but not allow the arms to exit the cockpit.

title: Attachment
text: Arm restraints shall be attached at the buckle of the driver harness when assembled. When the buckle is released, the arm restraints shall freely separate from each other and the harness buckle.

title: Head Restraint
text: A head restraint must be provided to limit rearward motion of the driver’s head from a normal driving position. The head restraint shall be a minimum of 19 mm (¾ in) thick. The head restraint shall be mechanically fastened to the vehicle, preferably to the vehicle frame. Hook-and-loop and adhesive methods are prohibited. Head restraints may also be mechanically fastened or integral to the driver’s seat.

title: Seats
text: The seat shall work in concert with the driver harness to secure the driver within the envelope of the roll cage. Seats shall be of conventional design. Suspension seats are prohibited. The seat back angle shall be between 65° and 90° from horizontal. See Figure B-30: Driver Harness Schematic.

title: Conventional Seats
text: Conventional seats shall be generally rigid and be of metal or composite construction (fibreglass or carbon fibre). Seats constructed of thermoplastic are prohibited. Conventional seats may also have a removable seat cover and/or closed-cell foam padding. The maximum thickness of the foam padding shall be 50.8 mm (2 in). Seats may be purchased from a manufacturer or constructed by teams.

title: Suspension Seats
text: Suspension seats, sling seats, hammock seats, or similar designs with webbing or cordage as the primary load path are explicitly prohibited.

title: Seat Design
text: Seats shall be designed to safely support the driver from the back and bottom. The firewall of the vehicle may not serve as any part of the seat.

title: Quantity
text: Seats shall have no less than six (6) total mounting points to the vehicle frame. A minimum of four (4) is required for the seat bottom plane. A minimum of two (2) is required for the seat back plane.

title: Arrangement
text: Mounting points shall be no closer than 152.4 mm (6 in) to each other, shall be designed to effectively secure the seat. Seat back mounting points shall be at or near the plane of the RRH and attach to the RRH or other tubes having met the requirements of secondary roll cage members.

title: Structure
text: Any tabs used to mount the seat shall meet the requirements of B.12.2 - Required Attachment Tabs. When mounting with tabs, direct contact of the tab to the seat is preferred, spacers up to 13 mm (0.5 in) shall be allowed. Any tube used to mount the seat shall have both ends terminated and be fully welded to other frame members. Any tube used to mount the seat with radial holes drilled in the tube shall be sleeved and reinforced per Rule B.3.6 - Drilled Members.

title: Rated Seats
text: For unmodified FIA- and/or SFI-rated seats, factory mounting instructions and recommendations may be utilised in lieu of B.4.5.3.1 - Quantity, B.4.5.3.2 - Arrangement, and B.4.5.3.3 - Structure. Factory mounting brackets shall mount directly to either the LFS, UST, RRH, or other tubes meeting the requirements of secondary roll cage members or to tabs meeting the requirements of B.12.2 - Required Attachment Tabs which are mounted to the aforementioned members. The factory mounting procedures shall be made available for review by the Technical Inspectors upon request.

title: Driver Equipment
text: All drivers shall wear required driver safety equipment. All driver equipment shall be in good condition and free from injurious defects.

title: Helmet
text: All drivers shall wear a properly sized motocross-style helmet with an integrated chin-guard. All helmets shall comply with one of the following standards: Snell M2020, Snell M2025, ECE R22-05, or ECE R22- 06. Any helmets not meeting these standards are explicitly prohibited. Figure B-39: Driver Equipment, Example Snell Sticker Figure B-40: Driver Equipment, Example ECE Tags

title: Type
text: All drivers shall wear motocross-style goggles with a full-circumference elastic band that wraps completely around the driver’s helmet. “Quick Straps” or other quick-release systems are explicitly prohibited.

title: Lens Protection
text: All goggles used by drivers must have tear-off or roll off lens protectors. These tear-offs or roll-offs are used to ensure the driver has unobstructed vision through their goggles. Teams must present their goggles and properly installed tear-offs or roll-offs at TI. Teams without tear-offs or properly functioning roll-offs are subject to being black flagged.

title: Neck Support
text: All drivers must wear a neck collar or a HANS device.

title: Neck Collar
text: Neck collars shall cover the full circumference of the neck, be in good condition, and be SFI 3.3 rated. Figure B-41: Driver Equipment, Neck Support

title: HANS Devices
text: The use of HANS devices is permitted in BSC. A HANS device may be used in lieu of a neck collar. All HANS devices shall be used in accordance with the manufacturer’s instructions. The HANS device shall show no signs of wear or other injurious defects. Motocross helmets may require modifications to apply tethers. Tether application information can be accessed at : https://www.trs-motorsport.com/pub/media/wysiwyg/cms/The-HANS-Device-Quick- StartGuide.pdf All devices that meet the SFI 38.1 specification shall be accepted as "Head And Neck Restraint System" devices. Caution: Leatt braces are not allowed due to the improper fitment of these devices with respect to nominal BSC seat design and seating position.

title: Expiration
text: Neck support (HANS devices or neck collars) expiration dates are not required.

title: Gloves
text: Drivers shall wear durable, abrasion resistant gloves to protect their hands.

title: Shoes
text: Drivers shall wear socks and shoes.

title: Upper Garments
text: Drivers shall wear a fire-resistant shirt or suit rated SFI 3.2, SFI 3.3, SFI 3.4, or FIA 8856-2000.

title: Lower Garments
text: Drivers shall wear properly sized fire-resistant long pants having an SFI, FIA, NFPA 2112, or other recognised fire-resistance rating.

title: Combustible Material
text: Jerseys, gloves, socks or other garments made from nylon or any other synthetic material which shall melt or combust when exposed to an open flame or extreme heat are explicitly prohibited from use during competition.

title: Fuel System
text: Note: Sections B.6.6, B.6.7, B.6.8 and B.6.9 are not applicable to BSC 2027 event.

title: Function
text: The fuel system shall safely contain, control, and convey all vehicle fuel. The fuel system shall compose of a fuel tank, fuel hose, fuel hose fittings, fuel filter, fuel tank mounts, the entire engine, and splash shields.

title: Fuel
text: The only fuel permitted for BSC competitions are grades of automotive gasoline consisting of hydrocarbon compounds. Commercially available Gasoline shall be made provided by the event organisers in the event venue at market price.

title: Location
text: The entire fuel system shall be located within the roll envelope of the vehicle. The roll envelope is tested by means of a straight edge in contact with any two points on the outside of the vehicle frame.

title: Fuel Cap
text: The fuel cap provided with the Rehlko CH 393-3153 engine is to be used.

title: Fuel Tank
text: Fuel tanks provided with the engine is not to be modified or relocated. The section B.6.5.1 is not applicable to BSC 2027 event.

title: Mounting
text:
Fuel tanks shall be mounted to a tube or tubes meeting the requirements B.3.2.3 - Secondary Members and Tubes. Tubes shall be supported at both ends. Cantilevered mounting is explicitly prohibited. Removable fuel tanks are explicitly prohibited. All mounting holes on the fuel tank shall be used to mount the fuel tank to the vehicle frame. Any and all fasteners used to mount the fuel tank shall meet the requirements in Article 12 – Fasteners. A rubber isolating washer, specifically McMaster Carr Part Number 94733A723, shall be used on each fastener, on both sides of the fuel tank mounting flange. A total of 8 rubber washers are required. Metallic washers shall be used on either side of the fastener stack-up, as shown in Figure B-45: Fuel Tank Fastener Stack-up. Metallic washers and bolts shall have a nominal fastener size of 9.525 mm (3/8 in) and washers to have an outside diameter between 20.625 mm (0.812 in) and 22.225 mm (0.875 in). Figure B-42: Fuel Tank Fastener Stack-up The preferred mounting is directly to two square or rectangular tubes with sleeved holes, and meeting the requirements of secondary tubes. Figure B-43: Fuel tank mounted to square/rectangular tubes (preferred mounting design) Figure B-44: Fuel tank mounted to "C" brackets. (Acceptable mounting design) Mounting to cantilever brackets (welded to a fully supported secondary frame tube) as shown in Figure B-47 is acceptable within the following requirements:
1) Maximum Length: Bracket length may not exceed 101.6 mm (4 in) from weld-line to centre of mounting hole.
2) Minimum edge distance: 14.29 mm (0.5626 in), measured from the edge of the bolt hole to the nearest outside edge of tab, and 9.525 mm (0.375 in) from the edge of the bolt hole to the nearest bend tangency. If using square tubing to form the brackets, minimum 31.75 x 1.6 mm (1.25 x 0.0623 in) tubing shall be used.
3) Allowable cross section: Brackets shall have a “C” cross-section. The supporting gussets may be tapered as shown in Figure B-48, and shall be a minimum 22.86 mm (0.9 in) tall at the weld. Flat brackets are not permitted. Figure B-45: Allowable Taper
4) Minimum Thickness: 1.6 mm (0.063 in)
5) Minimum Weld Length: At least the full outside face of the bracket must be welded to the supporting tube as shown in Figure B-46. Figure B-46: Minimum weld length
6) Lightening holes our cutouts other than the bolt hole are explicitly prohibited.

title: Location
text: All fuel lines shall be located away from sharp edges, hot engine components and be protected from hot engine components, chafing, or abrasion. Grommeting is required where the lines pass through any member of the vehicle. Fuel lines are prohibited in the cockpit. Fuel lines shall have sufficient slack to not be held in tension. Fuel lines shall be secured to fittings with SAE Size #4 adjustable metal clamps or Rehlko OEM clamps. Any breaks (discontinuities) in the fuel line, including those for fuel fittings such as filters, sensors, or cutout valves shall be located above the spill pan. The fuel line shall be continuous between the last connection above the spill pan and the Carburettor. The fuel line should pass around the spill pan or if the fuel line passes through the splash shield the fuel line shall be able to freely move up and down. Any attachment points below the spill pan not directly mounted to the engine shall allow the fuel line to freely move up and down. Note: To provide strain relief for the fuel line, it is recommended to attach a snug fit clamp to the engine that matches the OD of the fuel line. Example McMaster-Carr part #3177T52.

title: Rating
text: All fuel lines shall be SAE J30 rated fuel lines and bear appropriate OEM labels with rating information.

title: Size
text: All fuel lines shall be “3/16 in” (trade size).

title: Fuel Filters
text: A Rehlko in-line fuel filter is required and shall be located above the splash shield. No more than one (1) fuel filter may be used at a time.

title: Fuel Sensors
text: Fuel level gauges and sensors are allowed as long as the fuel tank is not modified. Fuel level gauges and sensors are allowed such that the capacity of the fuel system is not increased.

title: Fuel Pumps
text: Fuel pumps are prohibited.

title: Splash Shields
text: Splash shields are required to prevent fuel from accidentally being poured directly on the engine or exhaust while refuelling or preparing to refuel the vehicle. Splash shields shall divert spilled fuel away from the axis of the exhaust gases. For example, if the exhaust is routed directly aft of the vehicle, the splash shield shall divert spilled fuel to the left or right side of the vehicle. The splash shield shall be constructed of metallic material (greater than 0.5 mm or 0.02 in thick). Shields must be generally rigid, shaped such that any spilled fuel runs towards the outside of the vehicle, away from the exhaust, and does not pool on the shield or anywhere on the vehicle (including skid plates). An example arrangement of splash shielding is shown in two views in Figure B-47. Splash shields shall be mounted so they are engaged and effective at all times and are not adjustable. The splash shield must be mounted lower than the structural member supporting the fuel tank. The splash shield shall have a minimum clearance of 13 mm (0.5 in) to the exhaust system and shall not be impinged upon by exhaust gases. If the fuel line passes through the splash shield, it must pass through a sealed, grommeted hole in the shield to prevent fuel from leaking on the engine. Gland fittings are permitted. Bulkhead fittings are not permitted. Figure B-47: Fuel System, Splash Guard Installation Example

title: Fuel Containers
text:
All fuel must be transported in, and put into vehicle fuel tanks, from approved, unmodified containers. Approved, unmodified containers shall:
• Have a volume of 5.7 litre (1.5 gallon (US)) or less for fuelling vehicles during endurance event.
• Have a volume of 21.2 litre (5.6 gallon (US) ) or less for all other capabilities.
• Be equipped with an original cap to prevent spills when not in use.
• Be labelled with school name and vehicle number. Teams are required to bring all fuel to the fuelling zone during the endurance event, see Rule D.8.3.7 - Fuelling.

title: Fuel Tank Access Panels
text: To provide line-of-sight for track safety workers, an observer directly behind the vehicle shall have an unobstructed view of the fuel tank and associated components.

title: Brake System
text: The vehicle must have a primary hydraulically actuated friction braking system that acts on all wheels and is operated by a single foot pedal. The pedal must directly actuate the master cylinder through a rigid link (i.e., cables are not allowed).
