The brake system must be capable of locking and sliding all wheels, both in a static condition as well as at-speed, regardless of surface conditions or drivetrain mode. The braking system shall have sufficient braking force to hold the vehicle while the engine is running in any powertrain configuration used at competition. The performance of the braking system shall be subject to test upon request of TI at any point during competition. Failure of this performance test shall result in teams being required to return to their paddocks to make sufficient repairs before participating in further competition.

title: Brake Pedal
text: Brake pedals and associated components shall be constructed from steel or aluminium and be designed to withstand a minimum brake pedal force of 2000 N. The brake pedal shall have sufficient travel during a partial hydraulic failure condition. For bias bar and tandem brake systems, a single circuit failure can result in longer required pedal travel to actuate the braking system. The brake pedal shall be designed for unobstructed travel. Teams shall be prepared to show documentation and calculations of the pedal travel in failure modes showing a clear understanding of how far the brake pistons will travel. Unobstructed travel means that the driver can actuate the pedal in nominal and failure modes with a single motion. No obstructions are permitted that prevent the driver from applying their full force into the brake pedal.

title: Independent Circuits
text: The braking system must be segregated into at least two (2) independent hydraulic circuits such that in case of a leak or failure at any point in one system, effective braking power shall be maintained on at least two wheels. Teams are encouraged to construct each circuit to have its own physically separate fluid reservoir with a durable, resilient mounting. A dammed, single reservoir serving two circuits is currently permitted.

title: Brake Location
text: The brake(s) on the driven axle must operate through the final drive. Inboard braking through universal joints is permitted. Braking on a jackshaft through an intermediate reduction stage is prohibited.

title: Cutting Brakes
text: Hand or feet operated “cutting brakes” are permitted provided the section B.7.1 is also satisfied. A primary brake system must be able to lock all four wheels with a single foot. If using two separate pedals to lock two (2) wheels apiece; the pedals must be close enough to use one foot to lock all four wheels. Any and all brakes, when actuated, shall cause the brake light to illuminate.

title: Brake Lines
text: All brake lines shall be securely mounted to the vehicle and not project below the vehicle frame or suspension components. All brake lines shall be routed and oriented such that they are not pinched by steering or suspension parts, nor engaged with sharp edges. All brake lines shall have full range of motion within the steering and suspension system. At no time shall the brake lines be loaded in tension or become engaged with the vehicle’s tyres and wheels. All brake lines shall be designed for the pressures expected in the braking system and be chemically compatible with the brake fluid in use. No brake line may be constructed of plain plastic tubing.

title: Throttle System
text: The vehicle’s throttle system shall be capable of fully actuating the throttle arm to full throttle (100%) on the engine and of return to idle (0% throttle) when released. The throttle shall remain in the as inspected condition for the duration of the event. Re-inspection is available by appointment with Rehlko at the event site. “Throttle-by-wire” or other electronic throttle controls are explicitly prohibited.

title: Pedal
text: Only mechanical, pedal (foot) operated throttle controls are allowed. The throttle pedal shall actuate a throttle cable. Foot pedals shall be positioned to avoid entrapment of the driver’s foot when in any pedal position. Mechanical extensions such as thick pads or blocks may not be attached to the pedal or to the driver’s feet.

title: Pedal Stop
text: A substantial, mechanical, wide-open throttle stop must be mounted at the pedal. Body panels or other flexible materials are explicitly prohibited. The pedal stop shall be accessible during engine check and shall be set to not over-extend the Rehlko engine throttle linkage system.

title: Throttle Cable
text: The throttle cable must be covered (sheathed or jacketed) from the forward mounting point in the cockpit to the vehicle firewall. Rehlko recommends Rehlko designed throttle connections. If manufacturing your own throttle connection system to the engine, the connector to the throttle linkage arm must be pulled between ±5° from the linkage arm as not to impact the high-speed setting of the engine. Throttle cables may be of “bicycle style” construction where the cable operates only in tension (pull only). Throttle cables may be of “aircraft style” construction where the cable is capable of tension and compression (push-pull) operation. Severe redirections of the throttle cable at the engine or the throttle pedal causing binding or restricted function are prohibited. Redirections shall not exceed 15° from the cable jacket centreline.

title: Fail Safe
text: All throttle controls shall be designed to return to the idle-stop in the event of a failure.

title: Compressed Gas Systems
text: Compressed gas systems are only permitted for vehicle control systems. For example, a compressed gas system may be used to change transmission states (i.e. shift gears). Compressed gas systems are explicitly prohibited from providing increased engine power, cooling, and/or vehicle propulsion. The Technical Inspectors reserves the right to require additional protections or safety features on any compressed gas system.

title: Gas Composition
text: Compressed gas systems shall operate only with non-flammable or non-oxidizing gases. Air, nitrogen, and carbon dioxide are examples of acceptable gases. Methane, propane, and oxygen are examples of unacceptable gases.

title: Gas Storage
text:
Compressed gases shall be stored in containers meeting the following requirements.
a. Compressed gases shall be stored in cylinders (tanks) of proprietary manufacture, designed and built for storage and operating pressures, certified by an accredited testing laboratory in the country of the cylinder’s origin, and be labelled or stamped appropriately.
b. The compressed gas cylinder shall be located within the roll envelope and aft of the RRH, protected from rollover and collision damage.
c. The compressed gas cylinder shall be protected from damage from failed rotating equipment.
d. The compressed gas cylinder shall be securely mounted to the vehicle frame, engine, or transmission, and oriented such that the longitudinal axis of the cylinder is not in line with the driver.
e. The compressed gas cylinder shall be insulated from excess heat such as the engine or exhaust.

title: Gas Service Equipment
text:
All service equipment in the compressed gas system shall meet the following requirements.
a. Pressure Regulators shall be rated for compressed gas service and be mounted directly to the compressed gas cylinder.
b. Any and all fittings or connectors in the compressed gas system shall be rated for the pressures and temperatures experienced downstream of the pressure regulator.
c. Any and all hoses, tubing, or other conveyances in the compressed gas system shall be rated for the pressures and temperatures experienced downstream of the regulator.
d. Any and all gauges, indicators, or other instrumentation in the compressed gas system shall be rated for the pressures and temperatures experienced downstream of the regulator.

title: Compressed Gas Mechanisms
text: All compressed gas mechanisms, including cylinders, slides, actuators, or motors shall be rated for the pressures and temperatures experienced downstream of the regulator.

title: Design Objective
text: The cockpit shall be designed to protect the driver and permit easy egress in an emergency.

title: Cockpit Egress
text: Any and all drivers must be able to egress (exit) on either side of the vehicle within five (5) seconds. Drivers tested for egress time shall begin with all safety gear and be fully seated and secured in the vehicle with their hands on the connected steering wheel. Egress time is timed from the instant either of the hands of the driver is removed from the steering wheel to the instant the driver is clear of the vehicle. The TI shall select one or more drivers to perform the cockpit egress test. Drivers unable to demonstrate successful egress shall have their driver status revoked. Each team is required to have a minimum of two designated drivers.

title: Firewall
text: All vehicles shall have a firewall separating the cockpit from the engine and fuel tank compartments. The firewall shall be constructed of metal, at least 0.5 mm (0.02 in) thick. The firewall shall be mounted in the plane of the RRH and cover the area between the ALC and BLC. The firewall shall be mechanically fastened to the RRH. Fuel-safe adhesives are permitted in addition to mechanical fastening. Multiple metal panels may be used to form the firewall, provided there are no gaps between the joints. Select cutouts are allowed for control cables, brake lines, or electrical cables, provided the cutouts have proper grommeting and sealing. Large cutouts in the firewall are explicitly prohibited. Large cutouts include those for CVT ventilation, and other similar items. Air intakes may not penetrate the firewall and must remain within the roll envelope. Cutouts for drivetrain components are permitted.

title: Front or Mid-Engine Vehicles
text:
If the mounting points of the engine are completely forward of the RRH, the following requirements shall be met:
a. The fuel tank shall be mounted aft of the RRH and meet all requirements of B.6.7 - Splash Shields. The firewall within the plane of the RRH may also be considered the splash shield if the firewall meets all functional requirements of B.6.7 - Splash Shields.
b. The engine and any part of the fuel system forward of the firewall shall be completely separated from the driver and cockpit. The engine enclosure shall be metal and meet the requirements of B.8.3 – Firewall.
c. Engine enclosures must prevent fuel from spilling into the cockpit when the vehicle is in any orientation.
d. Any engine starting cords shall be extended and accessible without opening/adjusting engine enclosures. Starting pull cord direction shall face away from the driver.
e. All engine compartment venting shall be directed away from the cockpit.
f. The driver must be able to egress from both sides of the vehicle.
g. The engine enclosure shall have minimum clearance of 12.7 mm (0.5 in) to the exhaust components and meet requirements of B.2.7.14.1 - Muffler Clearance. The engine exhaust shall not exit in the direction of the driver and shall be shielded from contact by track workers and competition officials.
h. Placement and design of the engine and engine enclosure shall not impede access to the fire extinguisher. Notice: Track workers and event officials shall not open or adjust engine enclosures to access engine starting equipment. This may result in vehicle towing throughout the competition.

title: Body Panels
text: The cockpit must be protected with body panels that completely cover the area between the LFS and the SIM. No gaps can exist that are larger than 6.35 mm (0.25 in) and will be checked with a 6.35 mm (0.25 in dowel rod). These panels must be made of puncture resistant material, including plastic, fibreglass, metal, or similar material. They must be designed to prevent debris and foreign object intrusion into the driver compartment. The panels must be mounted securely to the frame with quick-disconnect fasteners using sound engineering practices (cable ties or hook-and-loop fastening is not acceptable). Quick disconnect fasteners include quarter-turn quick disconnect fasteners (i.e. Dzus, Camloc, Southco) or snap/pushbutton fasteners and be actuated manually or with simple tools. Rivets are prohibited.

title: Skid Plate
text: The cockpit must be fitted with a skid plate (belly pan) over the entire length of the cockpit, so that the driver cannot contact the ground and is protected from debris while seated normally. Skid plate material shall be metal, fibreglass, plastic, or similar material mechanically fastened to the vehicle. Skid plates shall be designed to prevent debris and foreign object intrusion into the driver compartment. Expanded metal, fabric, or perforated panels are not allowed. Skid plates extending aft of the firewall shall have features to prevent leaking fuel from entering the cockpit.

title: Linkages
text: All steering or suspension links exposed in the cockpit shall be shielded with a sturdy, robust, metal cover. The shielding shall be continuous and extend the full width of the cockpit (from the left body panel to the right body panel) and shall prevent the driver’s legs and feet from coming in contact, becoming entangled, or struck by the steering or suspension components during operation or a failure. No gaps can exist that are larger than 6.35 mm (0.25 in) and shall be checked with a 6.35 mm (0.25 in dowel rod). Note: Quick disconnect or easily accessible fasteners for cockpit steering & suspension covers are recommended and facilitate a faster TI Process.

title: Universal Joints
text: Universal joints in the steering system near the driver’s feet shall be shielded or sealed such that the driver may not become entangled in the joint. Caution: Loose shoelaces can and have become entangled in universal joints and steering parts and shall hinder driver egress from the cockpit.

title: Fire Extinguisher
text: All vehicles shall be equipped with a charged and functional fire extinguisher.

title: Rating and Required Features
text: All fire extinguishers for use on the vehicle shall have a minimum UL rating of 5BC. All fire extinguishers for use on the vehicle shall be equipped with a manufacturer installed dial pressure gauge. The dial pressure gauge shall be readily visible and indicate the unit has been properly charged. Each fire extinguisher shall be labelled with school name and vehicle number. Each fire extinguisher shall be equipped with an OEM-type pull pin and OEM-type retainer installed. Note: BSC 2027 requires design for specifications, team leaders may proceed with equivalent specification part providing proper justifications. The fire extinguishers are to be of rating to put out electrical and battery fires.

title: Quantity
text: Each team shall have two or more fire extinguishers meeting the requirements above. One fire extinguisher shall be installed on the vehicle, and the remaining extinguishers shall serve as spares.

title: Required Bracket
text:
The only permitted fire extinguisher mounting brackets are the:
• DV8 Off Road D-FIREX-MNT-DOR
• DV8 Off Road D-FIREX-MNT-S-DOR
• Drake FIREX-MNT-DAG
• Drake FIREX-MNT-S-DAG Note: It is recommended teams keep a spare mount available. For BSC 2027 requires design for specifications, team leaders may proceed with equivalent specification part providing proper justifications.

title: Mounting
text: The fire extinguisher shall be attached to the required mount with metallic hose clamps. The hose clamp mechanism shall not interfere with the access to the pull knob on the required mount. The fire extinguisher shall be oriented with the nozzle pointing towards the firewall and the dial gauge facing to the right side of the vehicle. Figure B-48: Incorrect orientation of extinguisher clamps.

title: Location and Clearance
text: The fire extinguisher shall be positioned on the right side of the driver, within the cockpit such that the fire extinguisher is completely below the driver’s eye-level, and the top half of the fire extinguisher is above the SIM. The fire extinguisher shall be easily accessible by track workers. The pull knob of the required bracket shall be easily actuated. To facilitate this, a minimum radial clearance around the pull knob of 63.5 mm (2.5 in) is required. It is understood the area aft of the pull knob shall be less than 63.5 mm (2.5 in) due to the design of the bracket. See figure for further clarification. Note: Radial clearance is the unoccupied space between the edge of the pull knob and the nearest obstruction. The measurement is not made to the centre of the pull knob.

title: Powertrain Guard Function
text: All powertrain components shall be guarded and shielded to prevent injury to the driver, trackworkers, or bystanders. Powertrain guards shall perform one or more of the following functions: protect against hazardous release of energy and provide pinch point and entanglement protection.

title: Hazardous Release of Energy (HROE)
text: Powertrain guards shall safely dissipate a sudden, hazardous release of energy from powertrain components in the radial and tangential directions. HROE guards shall be durable and mounted with sound engineering practices. HROE guards shall extend around the entire periphery of the guarded components.

title: HROE Guard Materials
text:
All HROE guards shall be constructed of one or both of the following required materials:
• Steel, at least 1.5 mm (0.06 in) thick, meeting or exceeding the strength of AISI 1010 steel.
• Aluminium, at least 3.05 mm (0.12 in) thick, meeting or exceeding the strength of 6061- T6 Aluminium. Figure B - 49 : Powertrain Guard Extent example on a CVT T

title: Belt, Gear, and Chain Drives
text: HROE guards shall be a continuous metal band extending around the entire periphery of the drive assembly. The width of the continuous metal band shall be wider than the entire width of the rotating component by a minimum of 12.7 mm (0.5 in) on each side. If the band does not extend the required amount past the component on one or more sides, the side(s) shall have HROE compliant guarding perpendicular to the axis of rotation, extending from the outer band to the shaft. A 6.35 mm (0.25 in) gap between guarding and shaft is permitted. Multi-part covers must have at least 12.7 mm (0.5 in) of overlap at joints along the periphery. HROE guards may contain ventilation ports along the path of the guard. Ventilation ports shall be constructed from the same material as the guard, be arranged in such a manner that no radial or tangential path exists for flying debris to exit the ventilation port. The ventilation port shall also be constructed to not allow a searching finger to contact the rotating components when the ventilation tube is removed. The guard shall enclose the entire periphery; ventilation openings are permitted only when they meet the specified debris-path restrictions.

title: Driveshafts
text: Driveshafts, also known as prop shafts, rotate at speeds faster than the drive axles and typically distribute power to front and rear differentials. A driveshaft consists of a structural tube between two flexible, power transmitting joints (universal joints, CV joints, or similar). A driveshaft may include a longitudinal slip mechanism to compensate for length changes. All drive shafts shall be constrained from failure via two drive shaft hoops, within 50.8 mm (2 in) of the 1/3 length point and the 2/3 length point. Hoops should have no more than 25.4 mm (1 in) clearance to the driveshaft. The driveshaft hoops shall be a minimum of 25.4 mm (1 in) wide and shall be mounted by welding or threaded fasteners. Hoop mounting must rigidly connect the hoop to the frame via material meeting or exceeding HROE requirements. Figure B-50: Driveshaft Guarding

title: Hydraulic Systems
text: Hydraulic systems shall protect against hazardous release of energy. Hydraulic hoses shall have jacketing that meets ISO 3457. Hydraulic relief valves shall safely vent to the tank and away from people. Any hydraulic hoses running through the cockpit to the front axle shall be protected from damage by a driver entering or exiting the vehicle. Protection shall be made by a sturdy, robust cover. Note that hydraulic systems shall meet the requirements of B.2.6.1 - Hydraulic.

title: Axle shafts
text: Axle shafts and associated CV or universal joints forward of the firewall directly connecting the front wheels/uprights to the front differential do not require specific guarding for track workers and bystanders but shall be separated from the driver and cockpit by way of methods meeting requirements of B.8.5 - Panels and B.8.6 - Skid Plate. All other universal joints, CV joints, or similar shall be protected with HROE guarding extending 25.4 mm (1 in) axially beyond the extent of the joint.

title: Pinch Points and Entanglement (PPAE)
text: PPAE guarding shall prevent clothing and/or searching fingers from contacting or becoming injured in rotating parts. PPAE guarding shall be resilient and be mounted with sound engineering practices. A standard 10 mm diameter cylindrical finger probe is to be used for inspection. Figure B-51: Powertrain Guard Example

title: PPAE Guard Materials
text: PPAE guarding shall be constructed from rigid, resilient materials. Fabric or other similar materials are explicitly prohibited.

title: PPAE Guard Features
text: PPAE guarding for belt, gear, and chain drives shall cover all directions that HROE guard does not protect. PPAE guarding may contain holes or slots for ventilation. Fastening methods may consist of threaded fasteners or quick release latches. Temporary fastening methods such as hook-and-loop fasteners, adhesives, or ratcheting tie-downs are explicitly prohibited.

title: Belt, Gear, and Chain Drives
text: Belt, gear, and chain drives shall have PPAE guarding.

title: Driveshafts
text: All driveshafts shall have PPAE guarding. Drive shafts (propeller shafts) connecting to rigid (solid) axles are exempt from PPAE requirements.

title: Axle shafts
text: Axle shafts and associated CV or universal joints aft of the firewall directly connecting the rear wheels/uprights to the rear differential are exempt from the requirements of this article. Portal hubs/uprights are permitted. Axle shafts and associated CV or universal joints forward of the firewall directly connecting the front wheels/uprights to the front differential do not require specific guarding for track workers and bystanders but shall meet the requirements of B.8.5 - B.8.6 - Body Panels.

title: Drivetrain Breather / Vent System
text: Gearboxes and transmissions using lubricants such as gear oil, automatic transmission fluid, or similar mineral oils shall be equipped with a closed system expansion chamber unless using an OEM sealed design. The expansion chamber shall be of the ATV bellows style and be properly sized to match the fluid volume and temperature changes of the system being vented. All components of the vent system shall be within the frame of the vehicle and checked in the same manner as the fuel system. Expansion chambers and connecting hoses or tubes shall be constructed from a material suitable for transporting the oil used in the system. At all times, the system shall maintain a clearance of 101.6 mm (4 in) from the exhaust. Relocation of the expansion chamber is permitted. If the mounting point of the bellows is higher than the muffler connection point on the engine, then the bellows must be relocated above the splash shield. Relocated bellows shall be attached to the frame structure with a tab and bulkhead style connection and be oriented no more than 30° from vertical.

title: OEM Guards, Unmodified
text: Unmodified OEM guards are acceptable for meeting the guarding requirements in this article. Any OEM, factory stock guards that are not modified are exempt from the requirements in Rule B.9.1 - Powertrain Guard. All powertrain components shall be guarded and shielded to prevent injury to the driver, trackworkers, or bystanders. Powertrain guards shall perform one or more of the following functions: protect against hazardous release of energy, provide pinch point and entanglement protection, or protect against release of lubricating oil from gearboxes. Hazardous Release of Energy. OEM covers must still meet the requirements of B.9.3 - Pinch Points and Entanglement.

title: Electrical System
text: A minimum electrical system comprising at least two engine kill switches, a brake light, brake switch, battery, and associated wiring is required. The vehicle electrical system shall be designed and constructed in accordance with good engineering and electrical practices. Brake lights, reverse lights and alarms shall operate regardless of kill switch setting. Brake lights, reverse lights and alarms shall be powered and functional at all times. Cut-out switches capable of interrupting power to the brake light, reverse light, or reverse alarm circuits are strictly prohibited.

title: Power Sources
text: The maximum voltage allowed for batteries and electrical systems on the vehicle shall be less 60 V DC or 48 V RMS AC. All power circuits shall have an appropriate means of circuit protection (breaker, fuse, etc.)

title: Batteries
text: Definitions: “Battery Cell” – The smallest building block of a functional battery. An electro-chemical energy storage device. “Battery Pack” – Multiple cells connected physically and electrically as a sealed unit. A battery pack may also contain a Battery Management System (BMS) to protect cells and aid in charging.

title: Cell Origin
text: Battery cells (of all chemistries) must be professionally constructed by a battery Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM).

title: Battery Pack Construction
text: If cells are lithium chemistry: Battery Pack shall be professionally constructed by a battery OEM. The original construction shall include a rigid enclosure (no shrink overwrap, or soft coverings) and shall include protection for both the cells and the BMS, if present. In case of teams constructing battery pack, invoices of the purchase of battery cells need to be shared with the BSC inspection team, In case of battery pack being bought, invoice of the same to be shared with the inspectors.

title: Series Use
text: Battery packs may be connected in series when installed on the vehicle.

title: Sealing
text: All battery cells shall be factory sealed and maintenance free. Batteries shall be incapable of being opened and serviced and not leak in the event of a collision or rollover.

title: Mounting
text: All batteries / battery packs shall be mounted with sound engineering practices and not come loose during normal operation, a collision, or rollover. Battery terminals shall be insulated and protected against an electrical short.

title: Chemistry and Charging
text: Permitted battery chemistries include: 1. Lithium: Charging of Li-ion batteries shall only be done off-vehicle using OEM chargers. 2. LiPo: Charging of Lithium Polymer batteries shall only be done off-vehicle using OEM chargers. 3. LiFePO4 (LFP): Charging of Lithium Iron Phosphate batteries with an integrated BMS (battery management system) from the vehicle alternator is permitted.

title: Minimum Voltage
text: All safety appliances, (brake light, reverse light, reverse alarm), shall be supplied with a minimum of 11 V DC. The voltage measured at the input terminals of each safety appliance, under normal operating load, shall not fall below 11 V DC.

title: Capacity
text: The power source for safety appliances shall have sufficient electrical capacity to maintain a minimum of 11 V DC for the entire length of the endurance event.

title: Shared Sources
text: If items other than safety appliances are on the same power source, engineering calculations and supporting documents shall be provided upon request to confirm appropriate sizing and capacity.

title: Engine Alternator
text: If an alternator is used, only approved engine alternators may be selected. See Rule B.2.7.16 - Alternator for further information.

title: Wire Routing
text: All vehicle wiring and connectors shall be cleanly and neatly installed. Wiring shall be routed away from sources of excessive heat, abrasion, chafing, and possible short circuit. Wiring shall be installed and routed such that it does not become a hazard to cockpit egress.

title: Wire Termination
text: Wires shall be properly terminated with appropriate terminals and fittings for all connections. Bare wire connections are not permitted. (i.e. bare wire under a screw terminal or clamp, wire nuts, etc.)

title: Connectors
text: Cable and wiring terminations shall have features to protect against reverse polarity connection. Note: Non- Polarised Connections don't require features to protect against reverse polarity connection. Note: Polarised Connections without features to protect against reverse polarity connection may be used provided they have adequate marking (Wire Colour, Terminal Colouring, Wire Number or Labels) to prevent reverse polarity connection.

title: Engine Kill Switches
text: Engine kill switches shall stop the engine without interrupting power to mandatory safety appliances.

title: Quantity
text: Each vehicle shall be equipped with a minimum of two (2) engine kill switches.

title: Required Switch
text:
The vehicle shall be equipped with one or more kill switches with specifications matching any of the following required switches for SAE BAJA:
• Polaris Part 4015321 or 4019114
• Ski-Doo Part 01-171 (http://www.mfgsupply.com/01-171.html)
• WPS 27-0152
• WPS 27-0154

title: Cockpit Switch
text: A minimum of one cockpit kill switch is required as defined by this Rule. Additional cockpit kill switches are permitted provided the switch meets Rule B.10.3.2 - Required Switch. The cockpit kill switch shall be mounted on the left side of the driver, along the SIM, within reach of a driver that is properly secured in the vehicle. No other push button switches may be mounted along the Left SIM. Restraining the driver in any way to prevent accidental contact is explicitly prohibited.

title: External Switch
text: One of the required kill switches shall be located within easy access to track workers on the right side of the vehicle, aft of the plane of the RRH, and forward of the right FABUP. The external kill switch shall be generally perpendicular to the firewall (±15°), the axis of the switch action generally horizontal (±15°), below named point BR, and no further than 177.8 mm (7 in), dimension “Z” in Figure B-5210.4.1.1, below named point BR, and shall be mounted on a tab connected directly to the RRH. The external kill switch shall not be recessed more than 50.8 mm (2 in) from the outside edge of the RRH tube. Figure B-52: Engine Kill Switch Mounting Position

title: Mounting
text: All engine kill switches shall be rigidly mounted to the vehicle frame with unobstructed access to the switch. All engine kill switches shall be free and clear of sharp edges or other hazardous conditions to track workers or the driver. All switches shall be mechanically fastened to the frame. Adhesives are explicitly prohibited. If any threaded fasteners are used to mount an engine kill switch, they shall meet the requirements of Article 12 - Fasteners. Any type of guard, cover, or obstruction to prevent accidental contact is explicitly prohibited within 76.2 mm (3 in) of the kill switch. Note: Rivets and other robust, captive methods are acceptable fasteners for fastening kill switches to the mounting tab. Technical inspectors shall evaluate each of these designs individually.

title: Signalling
text: Each vehicle shall be equipped with signalling devices. Cut-out or disabling switches or devices preventing the immediate function of the required signalling devices are strictly prohibited.

title: Brake Light
text: All vehicles are required to have a functional brake light to signal to other drivers the vehicle is stopping or slowing down.

title: Required Brake Light
text:
Only the following brake lights are permitted. Brake lights not listed are explicitly prohibited. Modification of the brake light from the OEM design is explicitly prohibited. All brake lights shall be configured to be fully illuminated when the brakes are applied, and completely extinguished with the brakes are released.
• Grote 54702, 54682, or 54672
• Grote 55202, or 55802
• Polaris Part # 2411099
• Polaris Part # 2411092-432
• Haul-Master – Part # 93263
• Command Electronics Part # 003-6018R
• Command Electronics Part # 003-6016 Note: For BSC, teams may proceed with equivalent specification part providing proper justifications.

title: Location and Orientation
text: The vehicle brake light shall have a resilient and durable mount and be positioned at a minimum of 1000.8 mm (39.4 in) above the ground. The vehicle brake light shall be oriented to be visible to trailing vehicles and shine parallel to the ground or at a slightly downward angle. Brake lights angled (aimed) above a horizontal plane are not permitted. The brake light must be visible at least at a 45° angle from the left and right of centre, for a total field of view of at least 90°.

title: Brake Light Switch
text: The brake light shall be activated only by a hydraulic pressure switch installed in the brake hydraulic lines. Each independent hydraulic brake circuit must be equipped with a hydraulic pressure switch. Cutting brakes are required to activate the brake light by way of a hydraulic pressure switch. Note: Mechanical switches, push or pull, are explicitly prohibited.

title: Reverse Light
text: Vehicles with a reverse gear shall be equipped with a reverse light. The reverse light shall illuminate when the vehicle is shifted to reverse gear and is extinguished when the vehicle is shifted out of reverse gear.

title: Specification
text: Reverse lights shall be marked with an SAE “R” on the lens of the reverse light and be of LED design, equal to or exceeding the SAE standard J759. Reverse lights may also be one of the approved dual function lights from B.10.4.1.1 - Required Brake Light.

title: Location and Orientation
text: The reverse light shall have a resilient and durable mount and be positioned at a minimum of 701.04 mm (27.6 in) above the ground. The reverse light shall be oriented to be visible to trailing vehicles and shine generally parallel to the ground.

title: Reverse Alarm
text: Vehicles with a reverse gear shall be equipped with an audible reverse alarm. The reverse alarm shall sound when the vehicle is shifted to reverse gear and silenced when the vehicle is shifted out of reverse gear.

title: Specification
text: Required reverse alarms shall be rated to meet the SAE standard J1741 or J994.

title: Location
text: Required reverse alarms shall be mounted to the vehicle frame aft of the plane of the RRH.

title: Instrumentation
text: Vehicles may be equipped with instrumentation to provide operational or performance information to the driver. All vehicle instrumentation must be included in the cost report.

title: Data Acquisition
text: Vehicles may be equipped with data acquisition (data logging) systems. Data acquisition systems providing feedback to the driver must be included in the cost report. Data acquisition systems not providing data to the driver may be excluded from the cost report.

title: Communication Systems
text: Teams are permitted to use radio-frequency (RF) communications systems. Any team using RF systems shall comply with federal, state, and local regulations based on the location of the event. At no point may a team’s RF systems cause harmful interference to the voice or data systems in service of competition officials or emergency responders.

title: Voice
text: Vehicles are permitted to use RF voice communications systems. RF Voice communication systems and equipment may be excluded from the cost report.

title: Data
text: Vehicles are permitted to use RF data communications systems. All RF data communications systems and associated hardware may be excluded from the cost report. Exception: If a data communications system provides feedback to the driver, it shall be included in the cost report.

title: General Requirements
text: Each vehicle must have towing hitch points at the front and rear, along its longitudinal centreline. These hitch points are used both for dynamic events and for vehicle recovery. Tow points must be attached to the vehicle frame and must allow for transmission of both longitudinal and lateral towing loads. Towing loads will be imparted to the tow point by way of hook or clevis. Tow points shall have sufficient strength to serve as a vertical lift point for the vehicle.

title: Front Tow Point
text: Front tow points shall be constructed of tubular steel, not to exceed 31.75 mm (1.25 in) and not less than 25.4 mm (1 in) in diameter. Tubing thickness shall not be less than 0.89 mm (0.035 in). Front tow points shall be mounted no higher than the vehicle’s SIM and not below the vehicle’s LFS. The front tow point shall be able to freely pass a gauge measuring 50.8 mm tall, 50.8 mm deep, and 203.2 mm wide (2 in x 2 in x 8 in) behind the front tow point tube. See Figure B-59 for further information. Figure B-53: Tow Point, Inspection Tool Fitment

title: Rear Tow Point
text: Rear tow points shall be constructed from steel and meet the following dimensional requirements. No lightening features or cutouts other than the hole are permitted. See Figure B-54 for further information. title: Fixed Rear Tow Point
text: Fixed rear tow points shall be fully welded to the vehicle frame along the base line, dimension Y. The tab may be vertically or horizontally oriented.

title: Swivel Rear Tow Point
text: Swivel, or hinged, rear tow points shall be attached to the frame by way of a swivel mechanism. A swivel rear tow point may be horizontally or vertically oriented. The tabs for attaching the swivel mechanism to the frame shall be fully welded, a minimum thickness of 0.125 in thick, and have equal base line weld lengths totalling greater than or equal to dimension Y. Swivel pins shall be a graded fastener at least a 0.25 in diameter meeting the requirements of B.12.1 - Fasteners.

title: Fasteners
text:
Fasteners in the following vehicle systems shall meet the requirements of this article.
• Driver Harness
• Fuel System
• Fire Extinguisher
• Engine Kill Switches
• Tow Point Swivels

title: Captive Fasteners
text:
Fasteners shall be made captive by the use of the followings:
• Nylon Locknuts
• Cotter Pins
• Safety Wire (for blind hole applications) Welded nylon lock nuts, lock washers and/or thread sealants do not satisfy the requirements of this Rule.

title: Thread Projection
text: To provide for proper thread engagement in the lock nut, threaded fasteners shall have at least two (2) threads projecting past the end of the nut.

title: Grade
text:
Threaded fasteners shall meet or exceed one or more of the following strength grades:
• SAE Grade 5
• Metric Grade 8.8
• AN/MS specifications Figure B-56 below depicts bolt markings meeting or exceeding requirements above. Figure B-56: Fasteners, acceptable markings

title: Proof of Grade
text: For fasteners without markings as described above, proper documentation shall be supplied which requires a purchase receipt and manufacturer’s specification (including markings) indicating the fastener strength exceeds or is equivalent to the requirements of B.12.1.3 - Grade. Note: Teams using fasteners with readily visible grade markings shall reduce their time in TI.

title: Unmarked or Custom Fasteners
text:
Any threaded fastener (threaded rod, eye bolts, titanium bolts, etc.) that is unmarked, or does not have any markings as listed, must be documented by one or both of the following:
• A purchase receipt and manufacturer’s documentation indicating the fastener meets or exceeds Grade 5 standards for that size.
• Equivalency calculations with a purchase receipt or test data showing that the fastener exceeds the strength for a Grade 5 fastener of the same size.

title: Modified Fasteners
text: Fasteners which have been modified in any way other than drilling for safety wire or shortening of the shank (threads) shall be proven to the BSC technical inspectors to meet the requirements of this article. In summary of section 12.1.4 and 12.1.5, Marked fasteners do not need any documentation. Unmarked OEM fastener requires documentation proof from manufacturer and any unmarked or custom or modified fastener needs engineering equivalency calculations.

title: Required Attachment Tabs
text: Tabs for attaching components in B.4.2 - Driver Harness, B.8.8 - Fire Extinguisher, and B.4.5 - Seats shall meet the requirements of this section.

title: Dimensions
text: Threaded fasteners used with required tabs shall match the nominal diameter of the mounting holes in the mounting bracket. For example, if a lap belt mounting tab is drilled for a 12.7 mm (0.5 in) hole, the fastener and the frame lap belt tab shall be 12.7 mm (0.5 in) in diameter. title: Construction
text: Tabs shall be constructed such that they do not visibly deform when loaded. Tabs shall be welded completely along the base line. The base line may be contoured to fit the surface the tab is welded to. Tab length will be evaluated as the distance between the mid-point of the base line and the hole centre. No cutouts or other weight saving features may be applied to the required tabs.

title: Vehicle Number Assignment
text: Vehicle numbers are assigned by BSC as part of the online registration..

title: Transponders
text: For BSC, a transponder system is used for timing and scoring. All BSC vehicles are required to have a transponder. Vehicles must carry a functional, properly mounted transponder of the specified type. Vehicles without the specified transponder shall not be allowed to compete in any event for which a transponder is used for timing. BSC 2027 organisers shall provide the specified transponders at the event site for a fee. All teams are required to avail this transponder. Use of any other transponder on the vehicle shall not be permitted. Any other transponder in addition to this transponder shall not be permitted.

title: Vehicle Numbers
text: Vehicle numbers are critical for the organisers and officials to positively identify team vehicles. Teams must design numbers to be visible in all race conditions or keep them clean and conspicuous. Numbers shall not be obscured by any other portion of the vehicle. Caution: Numbers that are not easily read may be black flagged and might not be scored during the endurance event.

title: Required Numbers
text: Three sets of primary numbers are required to be securely affixed to the vehicle. The vehicle’s number shall be readily visible from the left side, right side, and the front of the vehicle and strongly contrast with the number’s background colour. No leading zeros are allowed.

title: Required Font
text: Vehicle numbers shall be displayed in either the “Highway Gothic Regular” font or “Century Gothic Bold” font. No other fonts are permitted. Examples of both fonts are given below. Figure B-62: Approved vehicle number font examples.

title: Side Numbers
text: Side numbers, mounted to the left and the right sides of the vehicle, shall be mounted above the SIM and aft of the plane of the RRH. Side numbers shall not be visually obstructed by any part of the vehicle.

title: Front Number
text: Front facing numbers shall be affixed to the vehicle above the SIM. The angle of the front number shall be less than 45° from vertical.

title: Orientation
text: Numerals shall be aligned along a common horizontal line, and the entire number panels shall be mounted in a horizontal orientation (+/- 3° tolerance) to facilitate fast vehicle identification. The number panels shall have a minimum of 25.4 mm (1 in) and a maximum of 50.8 mm (2 in) spacing between numerals.

title: Number Size
text: The primary cutout numbers must be at least 152.4 mm (6 in) high, dimension “H” in Figure B-63. The primary cutout numbers shall have a stroke width in proper proportion to the font design for the given character height. The primary cutout numbers shall be mounted such that the projecting face is a minimum of 12.7 mm (0.5 in) and a maximum of 38.1 mm (1.5 in) from the background panel. Note: Avoid sharp edges or points on the inner and outer edges of the cut-out numbers.

title: Backing Panel
text: Each number on the vehicle shall have a highly contrasting background to facilitate easy reading. The edges of the backing panel shall be no less than 25.4 mm (1 in) from the edge of the numbers (dimension “C” in Figure B-69). Numbers may be outlined to provide enhanced contrast. Number backing panels must be securely fastened to the vehicle frame. Figure B-63: Vehicle Numbers, Example

title: Number Colour
text: Teams are free to select their own number and backing panel colours. Number colours must be a bright colour against a highly contrasting background and facilitate fast vehicle identification. The number backing panel shall be all one colour and all numerals shall be of matching colour. See Figure B-69.

title: SAEINDIA Logo
text: Two (2) SAEINDIA Logos must be displayed on the vehicle in prominent locations. These shall be distributed during registration at the competition.

title: Sponsor Identification
text: Teams may display advertising from their vehicle’s sponsors, provided it is in good taste and does not conflict with the vehicle’s number. SAEINDIA may require all entrants to display advertising from the competition sponsors.

title: Scoring Summary
text: All teams are expected to participate in all static judging and may be excluded from dynamic events if they do not participate in static events. title: Overview
text: All BSC vehicles shall pass a TI before they are permitted to operate under power. The inspection shall determine if the vehicle satisfies the requirements and restrictions of the BSC Rules. If vehicles are not ready for TI when they arrive at the inspection site, they shall be sent away. Teams sent away must prepare their vehicle accordingly and return to the inspection site ready for inspection. Any vehicle may be re-inspected at any time during the competition and correction of any non-compliance shall be required.

title: Procedure
text: TI shall consist of three (3) separate parts as follows:

title: Engine Inspection
text:
Rehlko Technical Representatives shall set the governors of all vehicles. Vehicles must be presented for governor setting with the engine output shaft bare and free of any objects, the drivetrain disconnected from the engine, the throttle cable disconnected from the engine, and functioning engine kill switches. Each vehicle engine must be inspected by Rehlko technical staff that shall:
• Confirm the engine’s compliance with the Rules and
• Set the governor to the specified engine speed (3,800 rpm) The engine inspection (with the engine installed in the vehicle) must be passed, before a team may apply for TI.

title: TI
text:
Each vehicle shall be inspected to determine if it complies with the requirements and restrictions of the BSC Rules. Each team must bring the following items to inspection:
• Frame Material Documentation: Receipts documenting the materials purchased, or otherwise acquired, and used to build the frame.
• Roll Cage Specification Sheet: A signed and completed copy of the Roll Cage Specification Sheet.
• TI Sheet: A properly completed TI Sheet.
• Drivers Present: All drivers must be present at TI. The TI must be passed before a team may apply for Dynamic Brake Check.

title: Dynamic Brake Check
text: At Dynamic Brake Check, both the external and cockpit kill switches shall be tested for functionality before the vehicle is allowed to proceed. If both switches pass the test, then the vehicle shall be dynamically brake tested. Each vehicle must demonstrate its ability to lock all four wheels and come to rest in an approximately straight line after acceleration run specified by the inspectors. If a vehicle fails to pass any part of the inspection, it must be corrected and brought into compliance with the Rules before the vehicle is permitted to operate.

title: Preparation
text: Teams presenting TI Sheets that are incomplete, inaccurate (i.e. do not correspond to the actual condition of the vehicle), are found to have four (4) or more items not in accordance with the Rules, or do not represent a serious effort at pre-inspection shall be denied inspection at that time and sent back to the end of the inspection line.

title: TI Sheet
text: Note: For BSC 2027, the TI sheets shall be shared via email to the captains.

title: Pre Inspection Requirements
text:
Before bringing their vehicle to TI each team must
• Pre-inspect the vehicle for compliance with the Rules
• Complete the official TI sheet (shared via email)
• Have the completed inspection list signed by the Faculty advisor and team captain.

title: Inspection Sheet Version
text: Teams must fill the most current version of the TI sheet within two (2) weeks of the competition and thoroughly inspect their vehicle in accordance with the TI sheet.

title: Inspection Stickers
text: A multi-part inspection sticker shall be issued in sections to each vehicle as each of the three parts of TI is completed .The inspectors will place the inspection sticker on the right side of the firewall above the driver’s shoulder. The inspection sticker must remain on the vehicle throughout the competition. Vehicles without all parts of the inspection sticker may not be operated under power. Any or all parts of the inspection sticker may be removed from any vehicle by the TI that has been damaged or which is reasonably believed may not comply with the Rules.

title: Modifications
text: Once a vehicle has passed TI its configuration may not be modified. All accessory components such as roofs, wings, bumpers, etc. are considered part of the configuration and must remain on the vehicle at all times.

title: Repairs
text: Approved vehicles must remain in “as-approved” condition throughout the competition. Any repairs of a part that is not identical as the broken part must be approved prior to the repair.

title: Non-Matching Components
text: Non-identical parts not approved will be subject to an appropriate performance penalty.

title: Tuning
text: Minor adjustments permitted by the Rules and normal vehicle maintenance and tuning are not considered modifications.

title: Support and Penalties
text: Teams not passing TI by 2:00 PM local time on the dynamic event day can avail support from BSC support team. Support availed shall be indicated by a sticker and penalty of this support is given in section D.1.1.

title: Objective
text: The objective of the engineering design evaluation event is to evaluate the engineering effort that went into the design of the vehicle and how the engineering meets the intent of the market, as detailed in the A.1.3 - Objective and the A.1.4 - Design Subject. Students will be judged on the execution of the product development cycle outlined in the Design Evaluation Procedures. Each part of the engineering product development cycle will be judged within the following subsystems: Suspension, Steering, Brakes, Drivetrain (CVT/transmission, front drive, prop shaft, front hubs, rear hubs, reduction box, and axles), Chassis, and Ergonomics. The Design Reports are to be submitted covering every stage of Engineering Design. Teams are reminded that BSC is an engineering design competition and that in the Engineering Design Event, teams are evaluated on their design. Components and systems that are incorporated into the design as finished items are not evaluated as a student designed unit but are only assessed on the team’s selection and application of that unit. For example, teams that design and fabricate their own dampers are evaluated on the damper design itself as well as the damper’s application within the suspension system. Teams using commercially available dampers are evaluated only on selection and application within the suspension system. A detailed list of Design Reports expected is shown in Appendix D.11.3.

title: Composition
text: The engineering design event consists of two parts: Design Evaluation and a Design Review Briefing (DRB) that shall be used as a part of the design evaluation.

title: Design Documents
text: List of documents to be submitted for Design Reports is mentioned in section D.11.3.

title: Scoring
text: The Design reports submission shall be worth a total of 550 points. Design Report 07 shall be evaluated in the Institution premises by inspectors before the final event. The DRB planned on the final event shall be for 50 points where the teams present their work in standard template. The judges may at their discretion award the highest placing team less than the maximum noted above. Design finalist may also receive bonus points that could make their scores higher than the maximum noted above.

title: Objective
text:
The purpose of the Cost Evaluation event is to provide teams an opportunity to show the cost/benefit design decisions used in the prototype vehicle. This aims to represent a comparable model for each team to be measured against. For BSC 2027 event, the target cost of the vehicle is ₹2,00,000/- for ICE BAJA. The vehicle cost in this case is sum of the following costs
• Vehicle including the front axle assembly, rear axle assembly, passenger compartment and Roll Over Protection System (ROPS)
• Powertrain (engine + Driveline components + Fuel supply systems)
• Seat, mandatory vehicle safety systems.

title: Cost Report
text: The Cost Report shall be summarized in an online format where teams can complete their overall Bill of Materials (BOM) with material and manufacturing costs.

title: Costing Sheets
text: For BSC 2027, the costing sheet formats shall be shared via email to participating teams.

title: Cost Documentation
text: Cost Documentation is required for all purchased components and material costs..

title: Cost Report Submission
text: Cost reports need to be related with Design Report submissions on vendor invoices. The cost presentation is scheduled during the final event.

title: Custom Component Costing
text: When a team incorporates a custom component into their design, whether manufactured by a third party or assembled from multiple off-the-shelf parts, the cost of the custom component must be based on the highest–priced individual component or equivalent off- the-shelf product used in its construction. For example, if a custom damper is built using a combination of low-end and high-end damper parts, the damper must be costed at the price of the high-end damper from which parts were used. This ensures that the costing accurately reflects the performance and value of the custom component in the vehicle.

title: On Site Evaluation
text: Teams may be required to meet with a cost auditor during the competition to ensure that the vehicle presented at the competition matches with the BOM submitted in the Cost Report.

title: Cost Audit
text: The judges may increase costs and/or fabrication times if they believe that the figures submitted are below current prices for the item, source, or process involved. All items found by the judges shall be added to prototype cost at three (3) times the price of items found missing or below current prices. Prices or times that are higher than the judge expects shall not be corrected. Teams that have entered multiple competitions will have penalties found during cost audit carried over to each subsequent competition that the team is entered. Mathematical errors will be penalized. Reports that are highly inaccurate, highly incomplete, or in which the costs cannot be substantiated, may be rejected in their entirety, leading to a score of zero for the Cost Event. Teams that are required to bring their vehicle to on-site cost judging must do so by their scheduled appointment. Failure to report by the scheduled appointment time will result in an automatic zero for the event. If teams need to reschedule their appointment, it must be done prior to their appointment.

title: Additional Team Review
text: The judges reserve the right to review with any team during the competition the accuracy of their BOM relative to the vehicle brought to competition. This includes teams who were chosen for audits as well as teams who were not originally chosen and notified.

title: Burden of Proof
text: During any audit or review, if a judge questions the cost, material, source, or manufacturing process cited in the BOM, the team is responsible for demonstrating the accuracy of their submission. The team must provide clear and convincing evidence. Teams must have all supporting documentation readily available in print or on a device with offline access during the on-site evaluation. Failure to provide sufficient proof when challenged may result in the items in question being re-costed at the judge’s discretion and could lead to further penalties.

title: Scoring
text: The Cost Evaluation event shall be worth 75 total points.

title: Points scoring
text: Difference of Cost (DOC) = Target Cost - Calculated cost of vehicle from BOM (₹) Target Cost = ₹2,00,000 ( for ICE- BAJA vehicle) If DOC > 0 , Cost evaluation points = 75 If DOC ≤ 0, DOC Factor (DCF) = (DOC) / 10,000 Cost evaluation points = Greater of ({0}, {75 + (DCF x 10)})

title: Cost Eligibility
text: Upon review of the data, the cost judge reserves the right to disqualify cost that has not been sufficiently validated (i.e. either through lack of documentation or outdated receipts), are determined to not be complete based on review, or are outside a reasonable level of cost based on the other vehicles in the competition (i.e. either too high or too low). The burden of proof is on the students, and the cost score shall reflect not only the student’s ability to properly articulate and communicate their engineering effort but must also be backed up by sufficient documentation.

title: Objective
text: The Business Presentation (BP) event evaluates the team’s ability to develop and deliver a comprehensive business, logistical, production, or technical case that shall convince outside interests to invest in the team’s concept.

title: Concept
text: BP concepts may change for each competition. The content of a team’s BP shall match the requirements of the concept. The team’s BP shall relate specifically to the vehicle as entered for the specific competition. Teams should assume that the judges represent different areas, including engineering, production, marketing, and finance. Teams should assume that not all judges may be engineers.

title: Tardiness
text: Teams that fail to make their presentation during the assigned time period shall receive zero points for the BP event.

title: Submissions
text: The BP concept may require information to be submitted prior to the event in Google Drive folder. Submissions may be graded as part of the BP event score. Pre-event submissions shall be subject to penalties as described in A.6.2.7 - Failure to Meet Deadlines.

title: Format
text: BP shall operate in a hybrid model consisting of a submission using Business Model Canvas template shared with teams. One or more team members shall present the BP to the judges. All team members who shall give any part of the presentation or shall respond to the judges’ questions shall be in the local presentation area at the time the presentation starts and shall be introduced and identified to the judges. BP’s shall be time-limited, and judges shall stop any presentation exceeding the time limit. Judges shall not interrupt the BP for questions. Any questions shall only be asked by the judges immediately following the presentation.

title: Virtual Presentations
text: No Virtual Presentations for BSC.

title: Onsite Presentations
text: All onsite teams shall present their BP to a panel of judges, and their score shall apply to all onsite competitions they are attending. Teams shall be ranked only against teams attending the same competition. Student teams may be required to submit a judge pre-read document ahead of their presentation. If so, teams will be notified ahead of time on the deadline and format.

title: Equipment
text: All audio-visual and/or communication equipment required for a team’s presentation shall be arranged and provided for by the presenting team.

title: Evaluation Criteria
text: Presentations will be evaluated on content, organisation, visual aids, delivery, and the team’s response to the judges’ questions. The actual quality of the prototype itself will not be considered as part of the presentation judging.

title: Scoring
text: The base BP score is a maximum of 50 points. At the judges’ discretion, the highest placing team may receive fewer than 50 points.

title: Bonus
text: In-person BP finals will take place at each onsite event for the top teams to potentially earn bonus points based on their performance. BP finalists may receive up to five (5) additional bonus points, resulting in a maximum possible BP score of 55 points where bonus points apply.

title: Training Programme
text:
Three (3) participants from each team are allowed to attend the training programme for each module. If two (2) participants attend the training programme for a module, ten (10) points (2 × 5 = 10) will be awarded to the team. If the same two (2) participants attend the MCQ module evaluation test and score more than 50%, fifteen (15) points (2 × 7.5 = 15) will be awarded to the team. Therefore, for each module:
• Training participation: Maximum 10 points
• Module evaluation test: Maximum 15 points
• Maximum score per module: 25 points

title: Overall Training Score
text: There are twelve (12) modules in the training programme. A team can participate in the training programme and evaluation test for all twelve (12) modules and can score a maximum of: 12 × 25 = 300 points Thus, the maximum Training Score is 300 points.

title: Alternative Certification Route
text: If participants are unable to attend the training sessions, they may attend the respective module evaluation test directly. To obtain certification in a module, a participant must score more than 90% in the evaluation test. If a team obtains twelve (12) certifications, with a minimum of one (1) certification in each module, the team will be awarded: 12 × 25 = 300 points The maximum score awarded for certification is twenty-five (25) points per module.

title: Equal Weightage of Modules
text: For each module, the team can earn a maximum of twenty-five (25) points only, irrespective of the number of participants attending the training or obtaining certification. Obtaining additional certifications in one or more modules shall not provide any additional points. All twelve (12) modules shall have equal weightage in scoring.

title: Safety Check
text:
At the staging area for each dynamic event, a safety check will be completed. This safety check is intended to verify the vehicle is safe to drive on the dynamic event course in its current configuration. This safety check may include, but is not limited to:
• Driver Restraint
• Kill Switch Functionality
• Brake System Check
• Governor setting (ICE BAJA) Failure of this safety check shall result in teams being required to return to their paddocks to make sufficient repairs before participating in further competition.

title: Objective
text: Organisers may or may not provide a practice track to teams. A practice track allows teams to test or tune their vehicle within the limits of the Rules.

title: Course
text: If the organiser provides a practice track, the course length and features are at the organiser’s discretion.

title: Procedure
text: After a safety check, vehicles are signalled to enter the practice track. After a predetermined time, set by the track worker, the vehicle is signalled to exit the practice track.

title: Penalties
text: Teams may be signalled to exit the practice track or barred from using the practice track if the track worker or competition officials observe unsafe conditions or behaviours.

title: Signals and Signage
text: See D.9.6 - Signals and Signage.

title: Scoring
text: There is no score awarded for practice.

title: Objective
text: The Acceleration Event is designed to measure each vehicle’s ability to come up to speed quickly from a standing start.

title: Course
text: Acceleration is measured as the time to complete a 30 to 50 m flat, straight course from a standing start. The course surface may vary from pavement to loose dirt. The choice of course length and surface are at the organiser’s discretion.

title: Procedure
text: After a safety check, vehicles are positioned at the start line of the course. The track worker shall check that the driver is ready to begin. Once the driver is ready, the track worker shall signal the driver to proceed down the course. After completing the run on the course, the vehicle shall be directed to the course exit. Each vehicle may make two (2) runs on the course.

title: Penalties
text:
• Stall At Start – Run Disqualified (DQ)
• False Start – Run DQ
• Driving off Course – Run DQ The organiser may modify the penalties imposed for different violations to account for differences in the length or design of specific event courses.

title: Signals and Signage
text: See D.9.6 - Signals and Signage.

title: Scoring
text:
The maximum number of available points for the acceleration event is 75 points. Scoring shall be based on the better of the two attempts. Timing shall be performed with an electronic timing system. The following equation shall be used for the acceleration score (Saccel): Where: tmin is the lowest (fastest) time by any vehicle trun is the time recorded for a vehicle’s run to be scored. tmax is the minimum of the following values:
• The longest (slowest) time by any vehicle, or
• 1.5 times tmin Vehicles with acceleration times that are more than 1.5 times that of the fastest vehicle shall not receive a score for this event. Teams attempting the event but exceeding the time limit shall be classified as “Excess Time.”

title: Objective
text: This event tests the vehicle’s relative ability to climb an incline from a standing start or pull a designated object, e.g. progressive weight skid, vehicle, or chain along a flat surface.

title: Course
text: The traction event may take place on a straight or curved course. The organiser shall determine the hill elevation (height), hill inclination (grade), and hill surface or object to be pulled.

title: Procedure
text: After a safety check, vehicles are positioned at the start line of the course. The track worker shall check that the driver is ready to begin. Once the driver is ready, the track worker shall signal the driver to proceed down the course. After completing the run on the course, the vehicle shall be directed to the course exit. Vehicles may not continue the attempt after they have stopped on the course.

title: Penalties
text: Driving Off Course – Score as maximum progress at point of exiting the course.

title: Signals and Signage
text: See D.9.6 - Signals and Signage.

title: Scoring
text:
The maximum number of available points for the traction event is 75 points. Scoring shall be based on the better of the two attempts. Timing shall be performed with an electronic timing system. If a vehicle cannot complete the course and get a time, it shall be scored on the distance that it travels before stopping. Once the vehicle stops moving forward the attempt is over and the attempt is scored for distance at that point. The following equation shall be used for the traction score (Strac): Where: tmin is the lowest (fastest) time by any vehicle trun is the time recorded for a vehicle’s run to be scored. tmax is the minimum of the following values:
• The longest (slowest) time by any vehicle, or
• 2.5 times tmin

title: Objective
text: Manoeuvrability is designed to assess each vehicle’s agility and handling ability over off-road terrain. Teams shall attempt to manoeuvre through the course with a minimum time.

title: Course
text: The course may consist of a variety of challenges at the organiser’s option, possibly including tight turns, pylon manoeuvres, ruts, bumps, drop-offs, sand, rocks, gullies, logs, and inclines.

title: Procedure
text: After a safety check, vehicles are positioned at the start line of the course. The track worker shall check that the driver is ready to begin. Once the driver is ready, the track worker shall signal the driver to proceed down the course. After completing the run on the course, the vehicle shall be directed to the course exit. Each vehicle may make two (2) attempts at the course.

title: Signals and Signage
text: See D.9.6 - Signals and Signage.

title: Penalties
text: The organiser may select a maximum of two (2) penalty types imposed for different violations to account for differences in the length or design of specific event courses. Penalties are times added to the total time a vehicle took to complete the course for a given run. The organiser shall announce penalties on their event website or at a mandatory team meeting. Penalties: One wheel outside the track – 3 seconds Two wheels outside the track – 6 seconds Three wheels outside the track – 9 seconds All four wheels outside the track – 12 seconds Driver skips the Pit cross – 20 seconds

text:

Only vehicles that complete the manoeuvrability course within a time not exceeding 2.5 times that of the fastest vehicle shall receive a score. If a vehicle is on the course for a time that exceeds 2.5 times the fastest time recorded to that point, then the attempt may be declared over, and the vehicle may be removed from the course and scored as “Excess Time.” Manoeuvrability scoring is based on the vehicle’s time to complete the course. Penalties are added to the vehicle’s time for a given run. The following equation shall be used for the manoeuvrability score (Sma): Where: tmin is the lowest (fastest) time by any vehicle trun is the time recorded for a vehicle’s run to be scored. tmax is the minimum of the following values:
• The longest (slowest) time by any vehicle, or
• 2.5 times tmin

title: Objective
text: The endurance event assesses each vehicle’s ability to operate continuously and at speed over rough terrain with obstacles in potentially adverse weather conditions, including rain. The endurance event may be run for time or for distance. In BSC 2027 event, the vehicle is expected to run for two (2) hours. The vehicle with most laps (orbits) around the course with fuel efficiency for ICE BAJA shall secure the maximum points.

title: Course
text: The endurance course is a closed loop measuring approximately 2 km. The endurance course shall feature different surfaces (e.g. dirt, grass, sand, mud, gravel, and stone). The endurance course shall feature various obstacles and terrain to test the vehicle’s durability, traction, and speed.

title: Pre-Gridding
text: Teams shall pre-grid before the endurance event and be placed into starting position based on each team’s performance in a previous dynamic event, or set of dynamic events, to be determined by the organiser. Pre-gridding shall close at a pre-determined time by BSC and the organisers. Teams late to pre-grid shall be gathered in the fuel area and released to the track after the race has started.

title: Compliance Check
text:
During pre-gridding, or after pre-gridding closes, vehicle engines shall be started, and the TI shall perform a compliance check. During compliance check and gridding, the driver and vehicle may only have one team member accompany them. The compliance check includes, but is not limited to inspection of the following:
• Helmet Certification
• Helmet Fitment and Securement
• Safety Harness
• Driver Equipment
• Driver Wrist Band
• Fire Extinguisher
• Engine Kill Switches
• Brake System
• 5 Point Seat belt
• Engine Calibration
• Driving licence and accident insurance Unprepared drivers or out-of-compliance vehicles deemed unsafe or not ready to drive shall be ordered out of the gridding line by TI and sent to the paddocks to make corrections. Vehicles not ready to drive must check in at the fuel area to be admitted to the track.

title: Gridding
text: Once the compliance check is complete, vehicles begin to form the grid and approach the start line as marshalled by track workers or Technical Inspector.

title: Starting
text: The endurance event may be started by a standing staggered start, rolling start, or hole shot. A standing staggered start is used to release vehicles in groups of two with a delay in between groups. A rolling start allows a run-in distance to the start line. The rolling start may be performed on the course. A hole hot is a start where all vehicles are lined up equidistant to the first course feature and started all at once. The start type shall be determined by BSC and the organiser. All vehicles shall be considered to have begun the race simultaneously at the time when the starter releases the first vehicle onto the course regardless of their actual position in the grid.

title: Running
text:
Endurance shall be run as either:
• A single two (2) hours competition
• A predetermined and published distance Vehicles shall safely navigate the course and accrue laps (orbits) to be counted and scored.

title: Driver Change
text: Vehicle drivers may be changed at any time. Driver changes occur in the Fuelling Area (FA). BSC reserves the right to require at least one driver change during the endurance event.

title: Location
text: No refuelling is permitted in the middle of endurance event. Only pre-event fuelling in ICE BAJA is permitted. Only three (3) people from any given team, including drivers, are allowed within the FA.

title: Procedure
text: Vehicles requiring fuel shall exit the track at the designated location and proceed at walking-speed to the FA. Before fuelling, the vehicle must be stopped, the engine shut off, and the driver completely out of the vehicle. The driver may not be tethered in any way, by harness, communications equipment, or clothing. Before fuelling, a team’s pit crew member must have a fire extinguisher ready and pointed at the fuel transfer point on the vehicle. The exiting driver is the only team member permitted to remove the fuel tank cap. A team fuelling their vehicle before the driver is clear of the vehicle or who fail to have a fire extinguisher present and pointed at the fuel transfer point shall be penalized. The fuelling area is to be clear of anyone not immediately servicing a vehicle. A fire extinguisher must be present and pointed at ANY transfer of fuel, including re-filling a smaller container from a larger one when a vehicle is not present.

title: Fuel Containers
text: Fuel shall be provided by the organisers in a specially designated fuel station in an Indian event. Teams are not permitted to bring fuel to the event. Fuelling will be done only in the designated FA. Any team found with fuel in the paddocks during the event will be disqualified from participation in any event and points earned thus far will be eliminated.

title: Repairs in Fuelling Area
text: No work requiring a tool may be performed in the FA. Teams are allowed to make adjustments that do not require any tools. Examples include driver harness, seat position, spring-damper preload, etc. Teams may only have approved fuel containers (see B.6.8 - Fuel Containers), fire extinguishers, and funnels, if required, in the FA. Tools of any kind, backpacks, wagons, extra driver equipment, and coolers are specifically prohibited. Extra driver equipment may be brought to the FA for use but extra driver equipment may not be stored in the FA.

title: Remote Pit
text: The organisers may elect to create a remote pit for the Endurance event. Any vehicle requiring minor repairs and adjustments can be attended to in a remote pit near the Endurance track.

title: Paddocks
text: Teams whose vehicle requires service and repairs may exit the track at the designated location and proceed at walking speed to their paddock. No repairs are permitted on the course at any time.

title: Recovery
text: Vehicles disabled on the endurance course may be recovered by track workers, or by a designated recovery crew. Track workers will attempt to assist disabled vehicles. It is the driver’s responsibility to assist and cooperate with the course marshals in removing the vehicle. Drivers shall not exit the vehicle to re-start the engine. Drivers must be seated and secured in the vehicle before track workers will attempt to restart the engine. If track workers are unable to assist a disabled vehicle, a recovery crew will transport the disabled vehicle to the paddocks. Drivers being towed to the paddock are required to remain seated and secured in their vehicle with all safety equipment on. Recovery crews are dispatched and operate on a “first come, first served” basis. No priority will be given to any team over another.

title: Finish
text: The Endurance event is finished when the lead vehicle crosses the finish line after the time limit or distance has been reached. Vehicles remaining on the track will be allowed to finish their lap. Vehicles in the fuel zone will not be allowed back on the track after this time. As vehicles cross the finish line, track workers will direct vehicles to the paddocks or the impound area (if required). All post-event traffic shall be at walking-speed.

title: Impound
text: BSC reserves the right to impound and inspect any vehicle during or after the endurance event. TI will direct and instruct teams in impound how to proceed.

title: Penalties
text: Technical Inspectors are the only personnel permitted to call and assess penalties during the endurance event. Technical Inspectors are distributed throughout the endurance course during the event. Penalties during the endurance event will be signalled from and vehicles ordered off the track from the black flag area. Technical Inspectors may stop any vehicle, at any time, if they believe it no longer complies with the requirements and restrictions of the Rules. All timed penalties are enforced from when the vehicle is in the black flag area, i.e. the time spent being towed back to the pits, does not count towards the penalty.

title: Driver Equipment
text: Any driver that is not using all of the approved and required drivers’ equipment will be flagged.

title: Mechanical Faults
text: All vehicles must remain in the as-approved condition in order to compete; any condition that is deemed to not meet this requirement will be flagged to make necessary repairs or adjustments. If a vehicle is stopped by officials for a mechanical fault, the fault must be corrected before it may re-enter the event.

title: Vehicle Assists
text: Certain areas of the endurance course have been identified as difficult obstacles. If a vehicle is assisted two times on the same obstacle, the vehicle will be black flagged and the driver warned that one more assist will result in removal of the vehicle for the remainder of the event.

title: Roll Over
text: If a vehicle rolls over longitudinally (end- over end), or laterally (on to its side) anywhere on the track two times (in any location, regardless of driver), the vehicle will be black flagged and the driver warned that one more roll over will result in removal of the vehicle for the remainder of the event. Roll overs will be judged at the discretion of Technical Inspectors. Any vehicle that rolls over must be inspected by Technical Inspectors before returning to the track.
