title: Points
text: The maximum possible points for endurance are 300 points.

title: Determination of Winner
text:
a. The team that completes the distance of the competition first or the greatest number of scored laps in the time set for the competition will be declared the winner.
b. In competitions of a given distance, the checkered flag will be given first to the leading vehicle, then to the other finishers as they cross the finish line.
c. In competitions of a timed length, the checkered flag will be given first to the leading vehicle as it crosses the finish line at or after the expiration of the specified duration, then to the other finishers in the order they cross the finish line.
d. If the leading vehicle is not running at the expiration of the time limit, the checkered flag will be given to the next highest running vehicle in the same manner.

title: Scored Laps
text: Scored laps are the number of full laps actually completed during the endurance event. Only full laps count; partial laps do not count for score. A vehicle must cross the timing line under its own power for a lap to be counted.

title: Finish Order
text: Finish order is the sequence in which vehicles cross the finish line after the lap scoring period has ended. Finish order determines the ranking of teams completing the same number of laps. For example, if the top four teams finish with the same number of laps, then they will be ranked 1st to 4th based on their finish order.

title: Scoring for ICE BAJA
text: The maximum points for Endurance event are 300. The score is split between lap-based score having maximum of 200 points and fuel efficiency, having a maximum of 100 points. Endurance score = Lap score (Sen) (200) + Fuel Efficiency score (Sf) (100) = 300 points. Endurance scoring is based on number of laps the vehicle completes in the allowed time: Total Score = Sen + Sf Where: Lmax is the maximum number of laps completed by any vehicle. Lteam is the number of laps completed by the vehicle to be scored. Lmin is the minimum number of laps completed by any vehicle.

title: Fuel Efficiency (100 Points)
text:
Fuel Efficiency (FE) scoring is based on the fuel efficiency achieved by the vehicle during the endurance event. The maximum score available for this event is 100 points. Every vehicle is filled with five litres of fuel at the start (fs) of the endurance event. The filling of fuel will be done by the organisers in the presence of the driver, captain and one other team member. At the end of two hours, fuel remaining in the fuel tank will be measured (fe). The fuel consumed during endurance shall be measured as (fs – fe). FE = Distance / (fs -fe) [km/l] 𝑆𝑓 = (100 × 𝐹𝐸𝑡𝑒𝑎𝑚 − 𝐹𝐸𝑚𝑖𝑛 𝐹𝐸𝑚𝑎𝑥 − 𝐹𝐸𝑚𝑖𝑛 ) Where: Distance = number of completed laps x length of track (2 km) 𝐹𝐸𝑚𝑖𝑛is the lowest FE by any vehicle 𝐹𝐸𝑚𝑎𝑥 is the highest FE by any vehicle 𝐹𝐸𝑡𝑒𝑎𝑚is the FE calculated for the vehicle. 𝐹𝐸𝑚𝑖𝑛 is the minimum of the following values:
• The minimum of FE value computed across all vehicles
• 𝐹𝐸𝑚𝑎𝑥 / 2.5

title: Safety Vision
text: Safety is the primary consideration in the design of BSC vehicles and the conduct of the competitions. No event or competition is so important that teams and organisers cannot take the time to work safely. All participants shall strive to create a safe competition where all participants return home in the same condition in which they arrived.

title: First Aid / CPR / AED
text: While medical services are always on-site at BSC events, teams are encouraged to be familiar with or trained in first aid, Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), and the use of Automated External Defibrillator (AED) machines.

title: Approaching Others
text: All participants are empowered to directly and respectfully approach others if they see a hazardous or unsafe condition and notify the person in danger. Persons approached regarding a safety concern are obligated to respectfully acknowledge the situation and are encouraged to thank those who approached them for their concern.

title: Responsibility
text: At all performance events, it is the responsibility of the team to ensure both the vehicle and driver meet and follow all the requirements and restrictions of the Rules. All team members shall be familiar with the location and operation of vehicle and paddock safety equipment, including, but not limited to driver safety equipment, fire extinguishers, and vehicle kill switches.

title: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
text:
Teams are required to furnish and use their own PPE, appropriate for the task being performed. This includes, but is not limited to:
• Safety Glasses
• Gloves
• Closed Toe Shoes
• Arc Flash Protection
• Hearing Protection

title: Key Hazards
text: All participants are encouraged to pay careful attention to the following situations:

title: Ascending and Descending
text: Maintain 3-point contact when ascending and descending stairs, ladders, steps, or tailgates. Watch for obstructions at the beginning and end of travel.

title: Pinch Points
text: Stay clear of pinch points from rotating machinery, doors, and other equipment.

title: Hazardous Release of Energy
text: Stay clear of sparks, chips, swarf, or other high-energy material. Check circuits for live wires before working on them. Depressurise high pressure air, oil, or water systems before working on them. Take care when working around presses, rams, or other hydraulic equipment. Use care when jacking or lifting vehicles or other objects.

title: Vehicle Operations
text: Do not drive when distracted. Utilise a spotter when backing a vehicle, especially with a trailer.

title: Walking / Path of Travel
text: Take care to keep all walking paths clear of slip, trip, and fall hazards.

title: BSC Vehicle Operation
text:
Any time the BSC vehicle is in motion, the following conditions shall be met: 1. Driver shall wear required equipment:
a. Driver Wrist Band
b. Eye Protection as per B.5.2 - Eye Protection
c. Helmet as per B.5.1 - Helmet
d. Neck support as per B.5.3 - Neck Support
e. Clothing as per B.5.4 - Clothing 2. Driver shall be restrained in the vehicle:
a. Safety harness as per B.4.2 - Driver Harness
b. Arm restraints as per B.4.3 - Arm Restraints 3. All required safety appliances shall be installed and operable

title: Engine Testing
text: In some cases, teams may need to start the engine with the vehicle elevated off the ground. Wheels are not permitted to spin/rotate while the vehicle is elevated for engine testing. The wheels shall be disconnected from the engine via mechanical means (i.e. removal of CVT belt, removal of driveshaft, removal of wheels etc.). Note: This Rule does not apply for any required functions such as engine TI.

title: Fuelling
text: When refuelling any piece of equipment (BSC vehicle, generator, hauler, etc.) the engine shall be stopped, and all people completely clear of the vehicle. Before refuelling, a team member shall have a fire extinguisher ready and pointed at the fuel transfer point on the vehicle. The fuel container and extinguisher shall be operated by separate individuals.

title: Sportsmanlike Conduct
text: All BSC participants can be proud of the excellent sportsmanship and cooperation among teams that are two of the hallmarks of the series. Good conduct and compliance with the Rules and the official instructions are expectations and requirements for every team member. Unsportsmanlike conduct can include arguments with officials, disobedience of official instructions and the use of abusive or threatening language to any official or other participant. Depending on the seriousness of the infraction the penalty for such actions can range from a deduction of up to fifty percent (50%) of the team’s points to expulsion of the entire team. Penalties of this type shall only be imposed after a complete review of the incident by the BTC.

title: Prohibited Material
text: Alcoholic beverages, marijuana, firearms, weapons of any type, and illegal materials are prohibited at BSC sites during the competition. The penalty for violation of this Rule is the immediate expulsion of the entire team, not just the individual(s) involved. This Rule applies to team members, Advisors and any individuals working with the team on-site.

title: Tobacco Products and Electronic Cigarettes
text: The use of all tobacco and marijuana products or using e-cigarettes on-site is prohibited.

title: Footwear
text: All individuals on-site shall wear durable and sturdy footwear. Open-toed shoes are explicitly prohibited.

title: Parties
text: Disruptive parties either on or off-site must be prevented by the Faculty advisor or team captain.

title: Housekeeping
text: Clean-up of trash and debris is the responsibility of the teams. Please keep the paddock area clean and uncluttered. At the close of the day, each team must clean their work area.

title: Site Condition
text: Please help the organisers keep the site clean. The sites used for BSC are generally private property and should be treated as such. Competitors are reminded that they are guests. All trash should be placed in the receptacles provided. Glass is not allowed on the grounds. Failure to clean the premises shall result in an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. Competitors are encouraged to clean their areas after meals.

title: Personal Transportation
text: The use of motorcycles, quads, bicycles, scooters, skateboards, rollerblades or similar person-carrying or motor driven devices by team members and spectators in any part of the competition area, including the paddocks is prohibited.

title: General
text: The organisers typically do not have a direct line of communication with spectators other than on-the- spot at the competition; thus, the competitors, Faculty and volunteers are expected to help inform the spectators of the safety Rules and help restrict spectators to the spectator areas.

title: Alcoholic Beverages
text: Spectators may not drink or possess alcoholic beverages at any competition location.

title: Access Restriction
text: Spectators must keep-back a specified distance from the event areas as decided by the BSC organisers and from any area where vehicles are operating under power. Motor vehicle competitions are potentially dangerous, and safety Rules shall be strictly enforced.

title: Children
text: A competition site is not a safe place for children and unsupervised young people. Spectators who fail to strictly control their children shall be asked to leave the site.

title: Expulsion
text: The course officials and organisers have the absolute right to restrict spectator access to any parts of the site and to eject anyone who violates safety Rules or ignores the instructions of officials.

title: Unsafe Conduct
text: All participants are required to exercise safe practices and avoid unsafe activities at all times during the competition. The BSC organisers and SAEINDIA have the discretionary authority to impose a just penalty for any conduct deemed unsafe. All team members shall be held to this Rule.

title: Team Vehicles
text: Only the BSC vehicles themselves and the teams’ support trucks and trailers are allowed in the paddocks.

title: Access Restriction
text: The organisers may limit the paddocks to team members, Faculty Advisors and competition officials.

title: Speed Limit
text: When a vehicle is driven anywhere except within the practice area or on event courses it must move at walking speed with a team member walking alongside at a normal pace. During the performance events when the excitement is high, it is particularly important that vehicles move at a walking pace in the paddocks. The walking speed Rule shall be strictly enforced, and discretionary point penalties shall be assessed for violations. At any point of operation, the BSC vehicles should not exceed 35 km/h. Over speeding shall first receive a penalty and repeated violations shall result in disqualification.

title: Escort Required
text: When a vehicle is driven anywhere except within the practice area or on event courses, it must have a team member escort the vehicle. The escort shall walk with the vehicle on the right side (to stay close to the firewall kill switch) and shall remain in the view of the driver at all times. The escort should act as a spotter to the driver, paying special attention to the vehicle’s blind spots and other vehicles. Under no circumstances may anyone other than the driver, ride in or on a vehicle. Escorts shall remain clear and not touch the vehicle when it is in motion and remain within line-of-sight to the driver.

title: Off Site Operation
text: During the competition, BSC vehicles may only be driven between the paddocks and an event site, during official practice, or in the events themselves and only after the vehicle has passed TI. Driving off site is explicitly prohibited. Teams found to have driven their vehicle at an off-site location during the event may be expelled from the competition.

title: Driver Equipment
text: Drivers not wearing the proper equipment will not be permitted to drive and may have their competition driver’s privileges revoked.

title: Meetings
text: All team members identified as captains or drivers, and all Faculty Advisors MUST attend all meetings as designated; Attendance at meetings is mandatory. Failure to attend meetings can result in disqualification of members or the entire team.

title: Pre Inspection Operation
text: Vehicles may not be started or driven prior to passing TI, except as required as part of the inspection process itself.

title: Signals and Signage
text: BSC competitions may use some or all of the signals and signage presented in this section.

title: Green Flag
text: a) When displayed at a starting line or when re-entering the course: The event has started; enter the course under the direction of the starter. b) When running on the course: Course is clear, proceed. Note: Green flags may also be represented by green lights at designated locations. Figure D-4: Signals and Signage, Green Flag

title: Yellow Flag
text: When displayed, there is a dangerous situation on the track beyond the flag station. Reduce speed and be prepared to take evasive action or stop on the track. Passing is not permitted, unless directed by the course workers. Note: Yellow flags may also be represented by yellow lights at designated locations. Figure D-5: Signals and Signage, Yellow Flag

title: Red Flag
text: When displayed, there is a dangerous situation somewhere on the track requiring a full-course stop. Come to an immediate, safe, and controlled stop on the course. Passing is not permitted. Pull to the side of the track as much as possible to keep the course open. Follow course worker directions. Note: Red flags may also be represented by red lights at designated locations. Figure D-6: Signals and Signage, Red Flag

title: Black Flag (Displayed)
text: a) Pull into the penalty box for a discussion with the TI or other official concerning an incident. A penalty may be assessed for the incident. b) Pull into the penalty box for a mechanical inspection of the vehicle; a dangerous condition has been observed on the vehicle. Figure D-7: Signals and Signage, Black Flag

title: Black Flag (Furled and Pointed)
text: Warning, the officials are watching this vehicle’s driving – obey the event Rules.

title: Checkered Flag
text: The event has been completed. Exit the course as directed by event officials. Figure D-8: Signals and Signage, Checkered Flag

title: Enforcement
text: Any violations of this article are subject to appropriate action by BTC. Actions may include, but are not limited to, a warning, removal of individual privileges (i.e. driver wrist band), expulsion from site (individual and/or team), loss of points, disqualification from the event, and ineligibility for future SAEINDIA events. BSC may also notify the Institutional administration for the team or individual in question.

title: Non-Endurance Events
text: Ties for non-endurance dynamic events will be broken by comparing the score of the second-best time or distance for the event in question. If the tie remains, the tie stands.

title: Endurance Event
text: Ties in the endurance event will be judged by the endurance event judge and may remain a tie.

title: Overall Event
text:
Ties for the overall winner will be broken in the following order:
1) Endurance Score
2) Total Dynamic Events Score
3) Total Static Events Score If a tie remains after the prescribed tie breakers, the tie stands for the overall winners.

title: Inspection
text: Any vehicle may be impounded and inspected anytime during the competition. Any vehicle found to have altered or substituted its parts or equipment since passing TI or an engine in violation of the Rules may receive a point deduction of 75 points each time it is found in violation.
